shigezane:090-293-1.title: Summary of a Letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa, July 16, Kan'ei (year unknown)
shigezane:090-293-1.summary: July 16, Kan'ei [year unknown]. Summary of a letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa. The opening reads: "Since then, there has been no word; I wish to hear whether the Lord Komon is in good health. This land remains unchanged. Lord Echizen is safe. May your heart be at peace..."
shigezane:090-293-1.markdown:
End

Since then, there has been no word; I should be most grateful to learn of your continued health and well-being. This land remains unchanged. Lord Echizen is safe and sound. I trust your mind is at ease. With all due respect, I present five curtains and five single garments. I offer these merely as a token of my appreciation. I trust you will accept them.

With utmost respect,

July 16

Kao of Tadao, Chancellor of Bizen

Residence of Lord Awa-no-kami Date

## Takemizu Note

Watari Date Family Historical Materials 119 (117) purports to be a letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa dated Genna 3, but it is actually from Ikeda Tadao, the Chancellor of Bizen.

In the text, Masamune's appointment as Chunagon (“Komon”) was in August of Kan'ei 3. Tadamune's title of Echizen-no-kami (“Echizen-dono”) was from June of Kan'ei 1 to April of Kan'ei 16. From August of Kan'ei 3, he concurrently served as Provisional Minor Captain of the Left Guard. Ikeda Tadao was appointed Sangi in Kan'ei 3 and died in Kan'ei 9.

Among these, Tadamune's stays in Edo in July occurred in Kan'ei 4, Kan'ei 6, and Kan'ei 8–9.

Additionally, the marriage between Furihime and Tadamune took place in Genna 3.

shigezane:090-467-1.title: Summary of a Letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa, October 9, Kan'ei era
shigezane:090-467-1.summary: Summary of a letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa, dated the 9th day of the 10th month of the Kan'ei era. The opening reads: "As per your correspondence, I have sent 10 shaku of rare kogo salmon from this area; I am truly grateful for your continued kindness despite the long distance. This land remains unchanged, and Lord Echizen is also doing well. ..."
shigezane:090-467-1.markdown:
End

As a token of my regards, I have sent you ten shaku of rare Kogo salmon from this area; I apologize for not being able to express my gratitude more often given the long distance. As for this region, all remains unchanged, and Lord Echizen is faring well. I trust you may be at peace. I look forward to hearing from you again in the future.

With utmost respect,

October 9

Tadao, Chancellor of Bizen

Residence of Lord Awa Date

## Takemizu Note

Watari Date Family Historical Materials 120 (118) purports to be a letter from Ikeda Mitsumasa dated Genna 3, but it is actually from Ikeda Tadao, the Chancellor of Bizen.

"Echizen-dono" Tadamune held the title of Echizen-no-kami from June of Kan'ei 1 to April of Kan'ei 16. From August of Kan'ei 3, he concurrently served as Provisional Minor Captain of the Left Guard. Ikeda Tadao was appointed Councilor in Kan'ei 3 and died in Kan'ei 9.

Among these, Tadamune was in Edo in October in Kan'ei 4, Kan'ei 6, and Kan'ei 8.

Furthermore, the marriage between Furihime and Tadamune took place in Genna 3.

The opening reads: "Yesterday the weather was exceptionally fine, and it was a great pleasure that Jibu Tasuke began his transfer. shigezane:090-833-1.markdown:

Furthermore, the day before yesterday, I was delighted by the feasts served until dawn. That is all.

shigezane:108.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 9, Tensho 15
shigezane:108.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 9, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "I deem it appropriate to convey my intentions via this letter; while I was instructing the courier, I received the reply. I have now examined it in detail. Accordingly, regarding the matter of the southern route..."
shigezane:108.markdown:
I deem it fitting to convey these matters via official letter; while dispatching a courier, I received the reply. I have now reviewed it in detail. Accordingly, I have received a general outline of the matters concerning the southern route. This is a most welcome development. However, we live in a world where one must remain utterly vigilant. Furthermore, regarding the key figures of Odawara to the south, and specifically the matters concerning the Satake domain, I have received detailed reports recently. Not limited to these reports, various matters have been brought to my attention repeatedly through confidential channels. Nevertheless, I shall convey the matters reported to me to you once more. 1. Regardless of the strategies employed in the world, your resolve must be your primary concern. 1. Beginning with Yasukojima, you must be most cordial toward the people along the borders. 1. Having stationed Shiroishi at Miyamori, it is only natural that you consult and devote your utmost effort to the affairs of the domain. 1. Regarding the matters concerning Tamai and Motomiya, there has been a persistent lack of progress, despite efforts to determine the appropriate deployment of 3,000 or 4,000 cavalry. 1. As those in authority and subordinates shall not be allowed to become complacent, you must show particular compassion toward the local inhabitants and peasants this year and next. 1. It goes without saying that you must prepare ample supplies of arrows, firearms, and ammunition. 1. Regarding the close attendants, their subordinates, and the general retainers, it is imperative that you exercise the utmost discretion to ensure no breach of trust occurs. 1. Takatama Omi-no-kami is also stationed at a vital stronghold of the great border; therefore, he must maintain his utmost vigilance at all times. 1. Even if various rumors circulate in the world, you must not be shaken. Furthermore, you must not let your guard down for a single moment. 1. You must first devote your utmost effort to the Tamura retainers without exception. Beyond that, I believe each of you should act according to your respective station. 1. Regardless of the specific details, you shall prepare the straw bales to be stationed at the borders as necessary. As we have long shared these matters openly and without reservation, I state them as such. The contents of this letter are, in essence, a matter of urgency. Once again, I offer these words with profound reverence and humility.

Postscript: Have you received word via this channel of the departure? It is entirely unrelated to that matter. Should matters proceed in this manner hereafter, I trust we can discuss them openly and without reservation, so that □□ may find peace of mind. That is all.

May 9, Masamune's signature

Lord Goro

shigezane:1120.title: March 12, Keicho 6: Document concerning Masamune Date
shigezane:1120.summary: March 12, Keicho 6: Memorandum from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "As a matter of the clan's interests, I place my trust in you; therefore, I hope you will have your views regarding the preparations."
shigezane:1120.markdown:
I rely on your loyalty and service; therefore, you shall have every right to offer your counsel. 1. Should you disobey my orders or act without military propriety, I shall not hesitate to expose such conduct; should you be informed of this by others, you shall be held accountable for your transgression. 1. Should quarrels or disputes arise, regardless of right or wrong, both parties shall be subject to punishment. The above, March 12, Keicho 6. Masamune (kao) To Date Hyobu-no-tasuke.

※A document of the same text addressed to Watari Mino-no-kami, dated the same day, also exists (Date Masamune Documents 1121).

shigezane:1199.title: Letter from Masamune Date, December 31, Keicho 7
shigezane:1199.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, December 31, Keicho 7. The opening reads: "I have been informed that Katakura Bitchu is to transfer to the lands of Shiroishi. Accordingly, you are expected to come to Watari. As for the details..."
shigezane:1199.markdown:
It has been decreed that Katakura Bitchu shall henceforth be transferred to the lands of Shiroishi. Accordingly, you are expected to come to Watari. Regarding the details, I have informed the Iwami-no-kami (Moniwa Tsunamoto). With all due respect.

(Keicho 7) Last day of the month, Masamune (kao), to Lord Iwa-no-kami

## See letter to Kagetsuna Katakura dated the same day

Regarding your own affairs, I shall proceed to the land of Shiroishi. As concerning the matter of that land, it pertains to the boundary, so please be understanding. It shall not be regarded as any irregularity if I instruct you based on my judgment. As for the details, I have provided them in full to Ishimi-no-kami.

(Keicho 7) Last day of the month, Masamune (kao), Kagetsuna Katakura

shigezane:122.title: Letter from Masamune Date, July 13, Tensho 15
shigezane:122.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, July 13, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "I have duly delivered the instructions. I have now presented them for your review. Since the night of the 11th, I have been uneasy regarding the attack. The forces guarding Ni (Nihonmatsu) and Shio (Shiomatsu)..."
shigezane:122.markdown:
I have formally submitted my report and presented it for your review. Regarding the attack that took place on the night of the 11th, I find it deeply concerning. It appears to have been the work of the guards from Ni (Nihonmatsu) and Shio (Shiomatsu). Concerning this, as for the Naeshiroda lands—have you taken any precautions? If they have been withdrawn due to that night's attack, I fear the public perception and reputation may be compromised. Guards should also be stationed there; above all, they should be secured as a matter of necessity. It would be prudent to place Shiba-miban guards at the front at all times. This has not been mentioned in the written report. I trust this has been understood as a matter of course. Regarding the matter of the firearms, I believe it would be most appropriate to dispatch them; however, as there is no immediate crisis, I wonder how the security for this autumn should be handled. Depending on the situation, I shall further propose the deployment of personnel. With utmost respect and humility.

Furthermore, it is appropriate that you proceed to Yasukojima on several occasions. As he is a man lacking discretion, there may be various matters that prove problematic. Since he is utterly unscrupulous, he should not venture beyond night attacks. Please give this matter careful consideration. That is all.

July 13, Tensho 15 — Masamune

Lord Goro

※Reply to [Shigezane's letter on the same day](#/post/shigezane/15-7-13)

shigezane:130.title: Letter from Masamune Date, August 24, Tensho 15
shigezane:130.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, August 24, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "I am profoundly delighted to receive your letter. I understand that you have established a residence in the vicinity of Naeshiroda. This is most appropriate. Next, regarding the construction at Hongu, yesterday."
shigezane:130.markdown:
I am most delighted by the news. I understand that you have established a residence in the vicinity of Naeshiroda. That is as it should be. Next, regarding the construction of the main shrine, yesterday—

Hain (Haneda Inaba)

I have now formally declined the request. I shall inquire as to the appropriate timing. Accordingly, as for Tamura Uma-no-kami (Tamura Kiyomichi), the Okoshi (Okoshi Kii) party, and others—those to whom I have separately communicated—it is imperative that you remain vigilant at all times. Should you let your guard down, any discrepancy may arise. I shall provide further instructions in due course. With utmost respect and deference.

August 24, Tensho 15 (Masamune's sealed letter)

Lord Goro

shigezane:135.title: Letter from Masamune Date, September 29, Tensho 15
shigezane:135.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, September 29, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "Having been away recently and not having heard news of your situation, I have been feeling uneasy; thus, your arrival is most welcome. Now, as for that place, O-bi (Ouchi Bizen) has sent word..."
shigezane:135.markdown:
Having been away recently and unaware of the state of affairs, I felt uneasy; thus, your arrival is most welcome. Now, as for the matter of Oubi (Ouchi Bizen), I have delivered the news. It is clearly stated in the document that you were granted an audience. However, my humble mind has been kept secluded. I humbly request further reports in due course. Accordingly, regarding the matter of Ta (Tamura), I have not given it any consideration whatsoever. You must by no means assume any understanding. Nothing shall be taken lightly. I shall explain each matter separately from this point forward. With utmost respect and deference.

(Tensho 15) 29th day of the 9th month, Masamune's signature

Lord Goro

shigezane:152.title: Letter from Masamune Date, November 9, Tensho 15
shigezane:152.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, November 9, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "I have hastened my journey. Now, regarding the matter of Kokubun, in response to the apology, a palanquin has been dispatched from Sugime to Niwasaka. I shall explain everything to Sugime in full at Yonezawa, and to Sugime, an... "
shigezane:152.markdown:
I shall hasten my efforts. Now, regarding the matter of Kokubun and the apologies, a messenger was dispatched from Sugime to Niwasaka. As it is more appropriate for my child to state his case in full at Yonezawa than to convey it to Sugime, I have arranged for him to stay at this temple. In due course, I shall explain the matter thoroughly and without reservation. No matter what objections may be raised, as I believe the handling of (Kokubun) Morishige is without flaw, there shall be no dispute. That such an apology should be made from Sugime—having been delayed from mid-summer to early autumn and now being pressed for an answer—is surely a matter that warrants understanding. That the matter was thus postponed, and that a difficult remonstrance was issued at that juncture, is utterly extraordinary. Based on your opinion, I request that the messenger be dispatched promptly to deliver the apology. If the timing is missed and the matter is unexpectedly diverted elsewhere, it may reach everyone, and I myself shall have to personally deliver the apology. I offer these words with utmost respect and humility.

(Tensho 15) November 9, Masamune's signature

Lord Goro

shigezane:1535.title: Letter from Masamune Date, July 17, Keicho 19
shigezane:1535.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, July 17, Keicho 19. The opening reads: "Regarding my journey south, I am pleased to have received the long-distance courier. While I intend to proceed to Edo in private, the Shogun (Hidetada) has first requested that I rest..."
shigezane:1535.markdown:
Regarding my departure, I take great pleasure in being entrusted with the long-distance courier service. While I had intended to travel to Edo in private, I have now departed abruptly, in accordance with the Shogun's (Hidetada) repeated instructions that I first take a period of rest. I shall explain the details in person in person. Respectfully submitted. July 17, Keicho 19. Lord Date Awa-no-kami

Thank you for the letter sent all the way here regarding my departure. I had intended to travel to Edo in private, but as the Shogun has repeatedly and earnestly instructed me to first get plenty of rest, I have departed abruptly. I intend to discuss the details in person. Respectfully submitted.

shigezane:1539.markdown:
We have not met since the other day. I shall make my visit in the coming days to engage in friendly conversation. Accordingly, upon my arrival from the capital, I have sent five saddles. I have sent these with the hope of meeting you in person. With utmost respect. Furthermore, I trust that the construction projects in Echigo (the construction of Echigo Takada Castle) are proceeding smoothly and to your satisfaction. [Seal] (August, Keicho 19) 8th day of the mid-autumn. Masamune (kao) "(Twist-sealed letter) From Masamune, at your lodgings in Ibushu."

shigezane:1587.title: Letter from Masamune Date, December 13, Keicho 19
shigezane:1587.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, December 13, Keicho 19. The opening reads: "It is most amusing that those in service should be drenched by tonight's rain. Nevertheless, I believe it will soon clear up. Therefore, as for the current situation here, from within..."
shigezane:1587.markdown:
It is most lamentable that those preparing for the occasion may be drenched by tonight's rain. Nevertheless, I believe it will soon clear. Therefore, as for the current situation, I intend to offer my apologies from within. Naturally, should the five or six days be needlessly prolonged, I most certainly shall speak up and voice my objections. Since I am preparing for that time, it is only fitting that you make preparations bit by bit. With utmost respect and humility. Furthermore, I observe that those in the Yamanote area are now about to arrive at the site of the preparations. Please keep this in mind and give your instructions accordingly. Respectfully. (Keicho 19) 13th day of the 13th month. Masamune's seal, Ifo-shu.

A rare letter written in a formal style. It was written in the midst of the Winter Campaign of the Siege of Osaka.

shigezane:162.title: Letter from Masamune Date, December 10, Tensho 15
shigezane:162.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, December 10, Tensho 15. The opening reads: "Regarding the matter of the Yasukojima estate, as I was informed the previous day, I have now received the full details in this detailed account. It is a most auspicious occasion of late. Generally speaking, as for the matter of that land, the 33 villages..."
shigezane:162.markdown:
Regarding the matter of the Yasukojima estates, as was reported the previous day, I have now received the full details in the written account. This is a most auspicious occasion. Generally speaking, while those lands are within the 33 districts, the fact that they were previously granted is well-known to the public. Furthermore, regarding the appointment and removal of Anji (Yasukojima Jibu), as stated, I believe it should be understood that no disputes shall arise; therefore, as this matter has been conveyed to him, I shall not elaborate further. Additionally, I have firmly instructed Morishi (Moriya Shiroemon) and Katako (Kagetsuna Katakura). As this concerns a vast territory where nothing may enter, it is only fitting that it be formally recorded. Above all, the full extent of your sincerity is manifested on paper. Though this is only the beginning, I am profoundly satisfied. Moreover, as this is a matter of great importance and difficult to resolve, around the 14th or 15th of this month—

Endo Suruga-no-kami

I shall proceed this way. There are matters I shall discuss with that party. I shall come without fail. I await your arrival. With utmost respect and deference.

10th day of the last month, Masamune's seal

Lord Goro

shigezane:167.title: Letter from Masamune Date, January 7, Tensho 16
shigezane:167.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, January 7, Tensho 16. The opening reads: "The auspicious occasion of the turn of the year brings no respite. Nevertheless, within the year..."
shigezane:167.markdown:
The auspiciousness of the turn of the year—there shall be no respite. Yet, within the year,

Endo Suruga-no-kami

At the time when matters were being exchanged, I intended to state my views on the matter of Arimasu's share. I find the timing most unsettling. Next, regarding the matter of the southern route, there are points I wish to make, so—

Toshun (Endo Suruga-no-kami)

It is certain that you will be surpassed. As for this turn of events,

Ha-u (Haneda Umasuke)

I am also aware. In that case, it would be appropriate for the two of them to proceed together. As for their departure, should the public sentiment be such that one is treated as being for my own use, I shall arrange matters accordingly and have them come. May your fortunes endure forever. With utmost respect.

January 7, Masamune's signature

Lord Goro

shigezane:1789.title: March 26, date unknown: Letter from Masamune Date
shigezane:1789.summary: March 26, date unknown. Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Today the mountain conditions were poor, and many deer were scattered, which is most regrettable. Given these circumstances, I feel that the entertainment here would be inappropriate; therefore, tomorrow I shall pursue the mountain..."
shigezane:1789.markdown:
The weather at Mount Kyoyama has been poor, and many deer have strayed, which is most regrettable. Given these circumstances, I feel that the entertainment here would be inappropriate; therefore, I shall order a hunt tomorrow. Even if it seems somewhat harsh, your attendance is most welcome. As I mentioned before, as there are no people nearby, your attendance is most welcome. I offer this with utmost humility. Furthermore, as I believe you ought not to remain there, I present you with a single jujube. Kakushi. March 26, Masamune (kao), Boshu, Oyado (place?)

Around the first half of the Keicho 10s?

Today's hunt yielded poor results; it is a pity that so many deer were missed. At this rate, even my recent diversions seem dull, so I have ordered another hunt for tomorrow. You may find it somewhat harsh, but please come and watch. As I mentioned last night, please keep your company small and come to the vicinity to observe. Respectfully and humbly. Furthermore, thinking you might not have one, I am sending you a jujube. Respectfully.

shigezane:1800.title: May 27, date unknown: Letter from Masamune Date
shigezane:1800.summary: May 27, date unknown. Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Since then, I have not written to you; I trust you must be finding it tedious during the rainy weather. It now appears that the weather will finally clear. Regarding your visit to the castle tomorrow..."
shigezane:1800.markdown:
Since then, I have neither written nor sent any letters; I trust you must be finding it tedious during this rainy weather. It now appears that the weather will finally clear. Tomorrow would be most appropriate for your arrival at the castle. I humbly submit this in my own hand. Respectfully and with utmost reverence. Though there is no particular cause, I have been silent ever since, as you see. [Seal] May 27, Masamune (kao)

(Twisted-seal Letter) Lord Iya-no-kami, Masamune

---

I have not sent any letters since, but I imagine you have been quite bored with the continuous rain lately. It seems the weather is finally clearing up. I hear you will be visiting the castle tomorrow. I understand you wish to meet and speak of various matters. With utmost respect and humility. There is nothing of great importance, but as we have not been in contact since then, I have written to you in this manner. Sincerely.

---

Sengoku BASARA-style translation (provided by MARIO)

Dear Shigezane.

It's been quite a while since I've written to you. It's been nothing but rain lately, so you must have been bored, right? It looks like the weather is finally clearing up, so please come to the castle tomorrow. I'd like to see you in person and catch up on everything.

It's not like I have any particular reason to write, but come to think of it, it's been quite a while, so I thought I'd drop you a line.

Well, see ya.

May 27, Masamune

shigezane:1809.title: July 12, date unknown: Letter from Masamune Date
shigezane:1809.summary: July 12, date unknown. Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Regarding Umatsumaru's departure, he has come here and reportedly inquired at the residence yesterday; we have left him satisfied. As I mentioned privately, I offered him some tea..."
shigezane:1809.markdown:
Regarding Umatsumaru's descent to this province, we have been informed that he visited us and inquired about the residence yesterday, and we have left him satisfied. As I have mentioned privately, I wish to offer him some tea; however, as there are few days remaining before the Obon festival, I shall visit him again at a later date. With utmost respect.

On the 9th, I came upstream to fish for trout and caught over 190. I would be most pleased to show them to you. Next summer, I most certainly hope to join you in person. I shall first offer my account in person. Respectfully.

July 12, from Masamune (kao)

(Twisted-seal letter) Ifusa-shu (Residence?) Masamune

Around Keicho 16–17?

Upon Umatsumaru's arrival in Sendai, he came here and visited the residence yesterday; I am also pleased. It is just as I had privately mentioned. I would like to offer him some tea and the like, but as it is just before the Obon season, there is little time. I shall save it for another occasion. With utmost respect.

On the 9th, I went trout fishing up here and caught over 190 fish. I would very much like to join you this summer. Let us meet in person and have a proper chat. Best regards.

shigezane:1892.title: Letter from Masamune Date, April 20, Genna 2
shigezane:1892.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, April 20, Genna 2. The opening reads: "I take great pleasure in receiving your special messenger. Accordingly, the Chancellor passed away on the 17th of this month at the hour of the Horse. As his will stipulated, we should offer our congratulations to the deity..."
shigezane:1892.markdown:
I write to you as a special envoy to offer my congratulations. Accordingly, the Shogun passed away on the 17th of this month at the hour of the Horse. His will stipulates that celebrations be offered to the deity. His remains are reportedly currently at a place called Kuno in Suruga. Thereafter, a temple is to be established on Mount Nikko, and he is to transfer there. The Shogun is expected to return to this area today or tomorrow. Shortly thereafter, he will descend to his domain. I offer my utmost congratulations. Respectfully and humbly.

Time and again, I have been fully satisfied with your communications at every turn. I am most pleased to receive 200 candles this time. That is all.

(Genna 2), 20th day of the 4th month. Masamune (kao)

Lord Awa-no-kami Date

I consider it a most auspicious occasion that you have gone to the trouble of sending a messenger. The Lord Chancellor passed away at noon on the 17th of this month. It is said that his will was to be enshrined at the shrine of Myojin. His remains will first be laid to rest at a place called Kuno in Suruga. Afterward, a temple is to be established at Mount Nikko, and his remains will be transferred there. The Shogun will return today or tomorrow. I, too, intend to travel to Sendai shortly. Let us discuss various matters in person. With utmost respect and humility.

Time and again, I am pleased to receive news from you on every occasion. I am delighted with the 200 candles this time. That is all.

Ifoshu, Guest House, Masamune

The day before yesterday, my mouth was exceptionally irritated and my tongue felt unbearable, so I was unable to meet you. Therefore, I wish to offer you tea on the morning of the 11th. Please bring Akimitsu Ishikawa along with you. With utmost respect and humility.

shigezane:1986.title: Letter from Masamune Date, June 4, Genna 4
shigezane:1986.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, June 4, Genna 4. The opening reads: "This morning, matters regarding Iwami (Maniwa Tsunamoto) were settled; I shall certainly speak with the four individuals. As for how it stands if we do not bring them together at once..."
shigezane:1986.markdown:
This morning, regarding the matter of Iwami (Moniwa Tsunamoto), I intend to have four men present to present their account. Believing that it would be improper not to do so all at once, I shall now personally dispatch four men to the Iwami site to provide a response. It should be that after a hundred days have passed, I shall descend; this shall be as decreed by you both. Furthermore, I intend to convey this in person. With utmost respect, (Genna 4) June 4, Masamune (kao)

Lord Yamato-no-kami, Lord Awa-no-kami

From Masamune

I believe you heard the grievances regarding Iwami from the four men this morning. In any case, I feel it would be unwise not to meet with them in person first; therefore, I intend to dispatch the four men directly to Iwami now to convey my response. Since a hundred days have already passed, I ask that you both strongly urge them to descend. Furthermore, there are matters I wish to discuss with them face-to-face. I offer these words with utmost humility and respect.

※ While the [Commentary] on the Watari Date Family Historical Materials dates from the time of Munemi's flight, it is a letter from Motsune Datemoto during the mourning period for Umamatsumaru. (Takemizu's Note)

shigezane:1988.markdown:
Yesterday, I visited Ne-no-Shiroishi for river fishing; the ayu I caught were somewhat large, and I presented several dozen of them. I hope you will enjoy them. I visited at an opportune time, making my rounds before the rain fell, and have now returned to the castle. I humbly submit these words as a token of my respect.

(Genna 4) July 7, Masamune (kao)

From Masamune, at the lodgings in Ifo Province

I went river fishing at Nebashiraishi yesterday and caught some sweetfish; as they are somewhat large, I am sending about twenty of them. Please enjoy them. I visited at a fine time and was able to return to the castle before it rained. Let us speak again when we meet. Respectfully and humbly.

shigezane:216.title: Letter from Masamune Date, March 8, Tensho 16
shigezane:216.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, March 8, Tensho 16. The opening reads: "Regarding that oral report, Shiro (Munemi Shiroishi) has sent a detailed letter. Since the Naeshiroda affair, I have continued to urge him to be prepared; now, how could he possibly waver...?"
shigezane:216.markdown:
Regarding that oral report, Shiro (Munemi Shiroishi) has sent a detailed account. Since the engagement at Naeshiroda, he has continued to instill that resolve in me; thus, nothing now moves him. As for the matter of the lower entrance, it hath been heard that—as if only now arriving—through consultation and coordination among the Ujiie party's Sansako and Tomizawa, many were slain, and over 300 wounded were captured on the enemy side, thereby achieving victory. Furthermore, the members of the outpost from Niinuma have each reported to me, offering their utmost loyalty. Regarding the matter of the witnesses having now crossed over to O(Osaki), the authorities have first handled the matter with great care at O(Osaki). As this is a matter of utmost urgency, I leave the rest to your discretion. With profound respect and humility.

March 8, Hour of the Boar; Masamune's signature

Lord Goro

shigezane:2182.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 17, Genna 6
shigezane:2182.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 17, Genna 6. The opening reads: "I trust this letter reaches you swiftly. As we have now been commissioned to undertake construction projects in Edo, while it is my sincere intention that we should meet in person to convey our intentions, ..."
shigezane:2182.markdown:
I trust this letter reaches you in haste. As we have requested permission for construction in Edo, while it is our sincere intention to accompany you and explain the matter in person, we have been granted leave and have no choice but to depart for the provinces. In the meantime, I have privately informed the Grand Cook that I should visit Edo around the end of next month to inspect the construction work. Upon my departure, I understood that you would arrange for a suitable attendant to accompany me; accordingly, I believe you were satisfied. However, I was firmly informed by the Grand Cook that since each member of your party would likely visit Edo upon our arrival, it would be absolutely unnecessary. Therefore, I intend to travel as a representative. While this is a grand undertaking, I shall prepare promptly to ensure your arrival is satisfactory. For further details, I shall consult with Shima and Daigaku. With utmost respect and humility: While I recognize the gravity of the situation, especially given the rainy season, not a single relative has been left behind for the public construction; thus, both the formalities and the actual circumstances dictate this course of action. Similarly, I request that you arrive in Edo by the end of this month. That is all. (Genna 6) May 17, Masamune (Kao) Date Bushu, Residence

I write this in haste via urgent dispatch. I had hoped to accompany you on the construction project in Edo, as I had intended to remain there to provide instructions; however, since you commanded me to return to my domain, I have had no choice but to return home. Accordingly, I privately consulted with the Grand Cook regarding a visit to Edo at the end of next month to inspect the construction work. The Grand Cook firmly informed me that if I were to visit after my return and with an appropriate attendant, you would, as you might imagine, be pleased. However, he cautioned that if I were to visit, the other daimyo currently away would likely do so as well; therefore, he insisted that my visit be absolutely unnecessary. Consequently, I now wish to send a representative to Edo. Though it is a grand undertaking, I trust you will make the necessary preparations promptly and that your visit will be satisfactory. I shall have Shima and Daigaku convey the further details. With utmost respect and humility.

P.S. I understand that requesting this during the rainy season may be an imposition, but it would be a matter of shame not to assign even a single relative to the government's construction projects; thus, I write as stated. I likewise request that you arrive in Edo by the end of this month. That is all.

shigezane:2186.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 21, Genna 6
shigezane:2186.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 21, Genna 6. The opening reads: "Though you visited me the day before yesterday and we should have spoken in person, as I mentioned in my previous letter, there is nothing particularly new to discuss, and in order to make preparations, a moment..."
shigezane:2186.markdown:
I intended to visit you the day before yesterday to speak with you in person; however, as I mentioned in my previous letter, there are no particular changes, and I intend to return as soon as possible to make preparations; therefore, there is no need for that. In the midst of this rainy weather, I believe it will be even more difficult to make arrangements. I sent word from Edo yesterday. As people will be arriving in succession, I now suggest that further communication may be unnecessary; nevertheless, there are still over 1,300 people coming this time. Please rest assured. I shall certainly report back to Edo. With utmost respect and humility. Furthermore, I join you in this great undertaking of your sudden visit. Taking the opportunity, I offer five layers of curtains and a supplementary note. That concludes my letter. May 21, Genna 6. Masamune's Seal, Ibo-shu's Residence.

Since you visited here the day before yesterday, I intended to meet with you in person; however, as I mentioned in my previous written notice, there are no particular changes, and since you likely have preparations to make, I felt I should return as soon as possible and ultimately decided against it. As it is a season of frequent rain, I imagine your preparations are quite demanding. I received word from Edo yesterday as well, stating that they are sending reinforcements as they come, so they said no further action is necessary; nevertheless, with over 1,300 workers coming this time, I am at ease. I intend to report various matters to Edo. With utmost respect and humility.

Furthermore, I believe this sudden trip to the capital is a most commendable undertaking. Fortunately, I have five layers of curtains at my disposal. Please accept this gesture. That is all.

shigezane:2192.title: Letter from Masamune Date, June 18, Genna 6
shigezane:2192.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, June 18, Genna 6. The opening reads: "Regarding the construction work at your place, I have sent further correspondence, as well as a letter to the three individuals, to follow up. The Shogun visited the construction site on the 10th, and..."
shigezane:2192.markdown:
Regarding the construction work there, I have repeatedly sent letters, as well as a single letter to the three parties, to follow up on the matter. The Shogun visited the construction site on the 10th and personally issued instructions to each of them; both the public perception and the actual facts are satisfactory. As the weather here has been poor for the past four or five days, I find it laughable to think that it would rain there as well. I assure you that no negligence has been shown, and I am fully satisfied. As for the Mimasaka matter, a consultation is forthcoming. I await news of a favorable outcome. With utmost respect. (Genna 6) June 18, Date Awa-dono

Regarding the construction work there, I have received your repeated letters, as well as a single letter addressed to the three parties. I understand that the Shogun visited the site on the 10th and personally issued instructions to each of you; this is a great credit and a source of joy for me as well. Here, the weather has been poor for four or five days in a row. I worry that it may be raining there as well. I am satisfied to hear that everyone is proceeding without negligence. Please consult with Mimasaka so that things finally move forward. I await good news. With utmost respect.

shigezane:2214.title: September 1, Genna 6: Letter from Masamune Date
shigezane:2214.summary: September 1, Genna 6. Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Regarding the construction at your place, I understand that the work has been slightly delayed due to the recent heavy rains, and I imagine you may be feeling uneasy. Now, as this is my first time visiting, I send one shaku of salmon. The road..."
shigezane:2214.markdown:
Regarding the construction work there, I understand that the schedule has been slightly postponed due to the recent heavy rains, which must be quite unsettling. Now, as this is my first time here, I send one shaku of salmon. I believe it is still fresh from the journey. I have not yet had my first diamond-shaped fish, so I have sent this. I have brought it from Watari. This is a welcome gift. I await your reply. Respectfully. (Genna 6) September 1, Lord Date Awa-no-kami

I hear that the construction work there has been slightly delayed due to the recent heavy rains, and I am concerned. Now, as I have received the first of the season, I send one shaku of salmon. I hope it does not spoil during transit. Did you send this along with the first diamond-shaped fish? I have had them prepared and sent from Watari. I consider this a welcome gift. Until next time.

shigezane:2224.title: Letter from Masamune Date, September 20, Genna 6
shigezane:2224.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, September 20, Genna 6. The opening reads: "I am most pleased to hear that the construction at your place is finally nearing completion, and that the layout has been decided. Above all, I regret that the various towns and districts have been damaged; as for myself..."
shigezane:2224.markdown:
I am most pleased to hear that the construction work there, and the layout of the fortifications, are finally nearing completion. In particular, I am glad to hear that the various districts have been repaired and that only my own domain remains undamaged; I am truly grateful for this blessing. Soon, once the restrictions are lifted and you descend, I shall certainly speak with you in person. Meanwhile, while you are away, I shall send some black cranes and firearms as tribute. They are of excellent quality. I look forward to hearing from you again. With utmost respect. (Genna 6) September 20, To Lord Date Awa-no-kami

I hear that the construction work there, including the layout of the fortifications, is finally nearing completion—how wonderful. I hear that various districts have been damaged, but I am grateful for the luck that only my own domain remained untouched. Once the construction is finished and you return home, I shall speak with you directly about various matters. By the way, while you were away, I shot some black cranes with a gun and sent them to you. They were delicious. Until next time.

shigezane:2267.title: Letter from Masamune Date, February 13, Genna 7
shigezane:2267.summary: February 13, Genna 7. Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "I write to you by urgent courier. Regarding the recent fire, as assistance from the Shogun, I have received 500 kanme of silver, and 200 kanme for the Mimasaka domain..."
shigezane:2267.markdown:
I hereby send this urgent dispatch. Regarding the recent fire, I have just been informed that the Shogun has graciously granted 500 kanme of silver as assistance, with 200 kanme to be sent to the Mimasaka domain. The public perception and the actual merits of this are equally great. As such, there is no need to express gratitude through the usual messengers. Though it is a great kindness, I wish to report this to you immediately. Your prompt preparations are most appropriate. As for the affairs of this year and such, I shall provide the necessary instructions, so please rest assured. I offer my utmost respects from Wakasa. With profound humility. I intend to report this to you around the 20th. I shall write to you again shortly. That is all. (Genna 7) February 13, Masamune (kao), Iboshu, Residence

I send this urgent dispatch by courier. Regarding the recent fire, I have just been informed that the Shogun has granted 500 kanme of silver as assistance, and Tadamune has also been granted 200 kanme. I believe this is a great honor and a matter for both of you to rejoice in. Therefore, as I feel it would be inappropriate to express my gratitude through the usual messengers, I apologize for the inconvenience, but I wish to send you as my envoy. Please make the necessary preparations immediately. I shall inform you of the points to keep in mind regarding the duties of the various officials for this year, so please rest assured. I will have Wakasa provide the details. With profound humility. I intend to have you depart around the 20th. I will contact you again shortly. That is all.

shigezane:2336.title: Letter from Masamune Date, August 21, Genna 8
shigezane:2336.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, August 21, Genna 8. The opening reads: "I hereby send this in my own handwriting. Today, the 21st, by order from the castle, regarding Mogami Gengoro—those of senior rank and juniors who have been dispatched to Edo for service..."
shigezane:2336.markdown:
I have formally submitted this in my own handwriting. Today, the 21st, a decree was issued from the castle regarding Mogami Gengoro; as he has departed from Suruga as a senior retainer to serve in Edo, the Lord felt it inconvenient and, despite objections among the retainers, ordered that Gengoro be protected at all costs, repeating this command two or three times. Nevertheless, the retainers failed to heed the order to protect Gengoro. In light of this, the Lord decreed that Mogami be punished according to His will, and appointed Honda Joshu and Nagai Ukon as envoys to bring him here shortly. Accordingly, a force of 3,000 men has been ordered. While this is a noble cause, I trust you will act as my representative. I humbly submit this. Together with horses and footmen, a total of 600 men should be brought along. Furthermore, I shall send Ojo Satsuma later to make arrangements. For now, this shall suffice. That is all. Date: August 21 (Genna 8) Masamune (Kao) Date Bushu, Residence

## The following are reference documents.

### Date Masamune Documents 2335: Letter to Ishimoda Daizen-no-suke Muneyori and four others

I have formally submitted this report. Now, as of today, the 21st, a decree was issued from the castle; while there are various objections among the Mogami retainers, the Lord, mindful of the success of Gengoro Chikasuru—who has departed from Suruga as a youth to serve in Edo—has repeatedly ordered that the retainers must protect Gengoro at all costs. However, as this instruction has not reached the retainers as a whole and they refuse to comply, it has been decreed that, under the Lord's will, punishment shall be imposed; accordingly, Honda Ueno-dono and Nagai Ukon-dono will be dispatched as envoys shortly. Accordingly, the Lord has ordered that 3,000 men be dispatched from your side to Mogami. Awa-no-kami-dono and Aki-no-kami-dono shall be appointed as representatives for the dispatch. The number of other personnel to be sent is listed above; please ensure the preparations are completed promptly. Of the 300 musketeers from your side, a provisional unit under the command of a magistrate shall be formed. Okuyama Daigaku shall oversee the deployment of these musketeers. Furthermore, Ojo Satsuma shall be dispatched within a day or two. At that time, I shall report the details thoroughly. Respectfully submitted. I have further dispatched this letter; may it reach Date Aki-no-kami-dono promptly. That is all. Subsequently, regarding Kojuro Katakura, as there are matters concerning the personnel and travel for the local residence, the number of men is as listed above. That is all. (Genna 8) August 21 Masamune (Kao) To Ishimoda Daizen-no-suke-dono, Moniwa Ryoan-dono, Suo-no-kami-dono, Yamaoka Shima-no-kami-dono, Okuyama Daigaku-dono

### Date Masamune Documents 2337: Copy of Letter to Date Aki-no-kami Sadamune

I hereby report this via urgent courier. Regarding the instructions issued by the Shogun, there are various difficulties and grievances among the Mogami retainers. Nevertheless, concerning the Mogami-Suruga matter, Gengoro has served in Edo since his youth. As he is the child of that house, the Lord finds the current situation regarding Gengoro to be inconvenient; thus, the Lord has repeatedly ordered that Gengoro be protected at all costs. However, as not a single one of the retainers has complied, it has been decreed that, under the Lord's will, punishment shall be imposed; accordingly, Honda Joshu and Nagai Ukon are to depart tomorrow or the day after. It is understood that three parties are to arrive at Mogami on September 8. Accordingly, the Lord has ordered that 3,000 men be dispatched from your side. Awa-no-kami-dono and you shall be sent as representatives. Please prepare a total of 600 men, including both cavalry and infantry, and proceed to Mogami according to the instructions of the aforementioned Joshu and Ukon-dono. Please consult with Boshu regarding all matters; that shall be most appropriate. Furthermore, Ojo Satsuma-no-kami will be dispatched later, and I shall report the details at that time. With utmost respect. (Genna 8) August 21 Masamune (Seal) To Date Aki-no-kami-dono

### Date Masamune Documents 2338: Letter to Kojuro Katakura Shigetsuna

shigezane:2520.title: March 30, Kan'ei 2 (?): Letter from Masamune Date
shigezane:2520.summary: March 30, Kan'ei 2 (?), letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "While there is no particular occasion, I write to you. My departure for Edo is set for the 9th. I trust you will understand. Regarding an auspicious day prior to the 9th..."
shigezane:2520.markdown:
Though there is no particular occasion, I write to you. My departure for Edo is set for the 9th. Please be advised accordingly. As there are no auspicious days prior to the 9th, I write thus. Having heard that you visited the office of Jibu-tasuke the other day, the various gifts—including the sashimi—were most extraordinary; we feel particularly blessed. I offer my sincerest gratitude. Respectfully and humbly. I shall write to you again later. Yesterday, I set out for quail hawks. Now, this year there has been a remarkable abundance of quail, the likes of which I have not seen in recent memory. As there were surplus catches, the number of birds was not as many as one might expect, yet I managed to catch as many as 40. It is quite strange that even a single quail's plume has risen. That concludes. (Kan'ei 2?) Last day of late spring. Masamune (kao). Iboshu, at your lodgings.

Though there is nothing of great importance, I write to you. My departure for Edo is set for the 9th, so please keep that in mind. There are no auspicious days prior to the 9th, which is why it has been arranged. Now, upon hearing that I was visiting the office of Jibu the other day, I found the various tokens of kindness—including the sashimi—to be most extraordinary. I was truly delighted. Let us meet again and speak. Respectfully and humbly. Postscript: Yesterday, I went out for quail hawks. Now, the abundance of quail this year is unlike anything I have remembered in recent years. Even with the nets cast, there were too many to catch; I did not get as many as I had hoped, yet I still managed to catch 40. Perhaps the plumes of the quail have risen slightly. It is quite interesting. That is all.

shigezane:2547.title: Letter from Masamune Date, August 27, Kan'ei 2
shigezane:2547.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, August 27, Kan'ei 2. The opening reads: "The first black crane has been delivered; it has just arrived at the hour of the Snake. This is because I have always been deeply mindful of it. I shall present it to the Shogun...."
shigezane:2547.markdown:
The first black crane has been presented to me; it has arrived just now at the hour of the Snake. This is because I have always remained deeply mindful of it. I shall present it to the Shogun. I have just departed for Ryugasaki and have seen that land for the first time. Upon my arrival, the Ogosho commanded that I be sent here along the way to comfort me, and I was granted a magnificent nesting site—a great blessing. I offer my most humble and respectful regards. Furthermore, the repeated offerings of hishi-gui and this latest crane are most precious and satisfying. That is all. (Kan'ei 2) August 27. Masamune's seal. Lord Awa-no-kami.

The first black crane you sent has arrived just now, at the hour of the Snake. This is surely because you have always been so attentive. I have immediately presented it to the Shogun (Iemitsu). Recently, I was granted leave to go to Ryugasaki and saw that land for the first time. Upon my arrival here, the Ogosho (Hidetada) commanded that I enjoy falconry along the way and in Ryugasaki, and I received two magnificent male hawks. It is a great blessing. I offer my most humble and respectful regards. Furthermore, both the repeated offerings of hishi-gui and this crane are most precious and satisfying. That is all.

shigezane:2561.title: Letter from Masamune Date, October 11, Kan'ei 2
shigezane:2561.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, October 11, Kan'ei 2. The opening reads: "Recently, Kayaba Genbei was brought before me; I inquired directly about the condition of the firearms. Although he has no master, through natural training, he will surely become proficient..."
shigezane:2561.markdown:
Recently, Genbei Kayaba was brought before me, and I personally inquired about the condition of his musket. Although he has no master, I assessed that through natural training, he must surely possess the appropriate proficiency; and indeed, he proved to be so. I find this most remarkable. This is in accordance with the Inatomi school. As I wish to recount the tale of Genbei in full, I cannot do so here. With utmost respect.

(Kan'ei 2) October 11, Lord Awa-no-kami Date

Regarding the matter of sending Kayaba Genbei to Edo, I inquired with Genbei directly about the firearms. I had thought that for one to become so proficient through their own training, even without a master, must be quite an extraordinary feat—and indeed, it was. It is truly remarkable. I understand it is the Inatomi style. I shall have Genbei convey the details, so this will suffice. With utmost respect and deference.

shigezane:257.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 6, Tensho 16
shigezane:257.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 6, Tensho 16. The opening reads: "Recently, I have been making successive representations through Han-in (Haneda Inaba). Around the 10th, I intended to send someone out, but the timing was not auspicious..."
shigezane:257.markdown:
Recently, I have been making gradual arrangements via Hain (Haneda Inaba). I intended to have them depart privately around the 10th, but as the timing proved unfavorable, I am prepared to set out without fail on the 14th. Accordingly, have all the members of the Aizu party returned home? Additionally, I wish to inquire about the situation at the Asaka (Asaka) entrance. As for this entrance, there have been no incidents as of late. Furthermore, on the 28th of last month, over 50 members of the Mogami (Mogami) party were captured at the Akiu border. Subsequently, I sent troops from Kokubun to the Mogami-Kurokawa border and captured over 10 people. Victories have been achieved in various locations. I believe you shall be satisfied.

May 6, Tensho 16 (Masamune [kao])

Lord Goro

shigezane:29.title: Copy of a letter by Masamune Date, November 17, Tensho 13
shigezane:29.summary: Copy of a letter by Masamune Date, dated November 17, Tensho 13. It begins: "Now, today, in the battle at the Kannon Hall, with your small force, you engaged the enemy—who had the enemy at their backs and were aided by a large army from Arai—and fought in a manner unparalleled..."
shigezane:29.markdown:
Now, today, in the battle at the Kannon Hall, you engaged the great army—with the enemy at your rear and reinforcements arriving from Arai—with your own small force; your feat was unparalleled, and you achieved such great success that it defies all expectation, astonishing all who hear of it. I am deeply pleased that, through your personal leadership, you have aided the various forces. Nevertheless, it is utterly laughable that there must be so many dead and wounded among your retainers. I hear that tomorrow, you shall advance close to the enemy camp at the main shrine. If you can indeed reach that place, it would be your greatest wish. I have also conveyed this intent to Date Ueno-no-kami Masakage. With utmost respect and humility.

(Tensho 13) November 17, Hour of the Boar: Masamune's Messenger, Yamaji Awaji-dono

※ In the "Watari Date Family Historical Materials" (29 original Masamune documents held by Date City, Hokkaido), the closing phrase is "Kyoko Kingen." The reading above follows the entry in *History of Sendai City: Masamune Documents 29*.

## References

**[Masamune-ki: "Battle of Motomiya and the Hitoribashi Engagement"](#/post/shigezane/masamuneki2-4)**

"To begin with, today a battle took place at the Kannon Hall; while a large force—having retreated from Arai and arrived once more at the Kannon Hall—engaged you and your small contingent, you, despite being outnumbered, achieved a great victory and a feat of unparalleled honor, astonishing all who heard the news. Due to your personal conduct, the various armies are immensely pleased; yet, it is utterly laughable that there should be so many wounded and dead among your retainers. I have heard that tomorrow the enemy army is to take up positions near Motomiya; should you be able to proceed to that location, it would be your greatest wish. I have also conveyed this to Masakage Date of Ueno, who concurred with the sentiment. On the hour of the Boar, November 17th, Shigezane, Masamune."

**[Shigezane-ki: "1. On the night of the 17th, Lord Masamune..."](#/post/shigezane/shigezaneki-16)**

In the formal address, he also stated: "Today's conduct is without parallel. To have fought behind the enemy's lines and not succumbed to the defeated army is unprecedented. Precisely because of your actions, many have come to safety. Surely there will be numerous wounded and dead. In particular, I have heard that tomorrow, the enemy will advance toward the main shrine. Though some may wish to be dispatched, as none are left, I shall enter the main shrine, albeit out of a sense of duty. Date Ueno has been dispatched." Thus he commanded.

shigezane:3205.title: Letter from Masamune Date, intercalary 10th month, 14th day, Kan'ei 8
shigezane:3205.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, intercalary 10th month, 14th day, Kan'ei 8. The opening reads: "The crane—of which there has been none here until now—has arrived; this is a rare occurrence, most especially a cause for great joy. Next month, around the 10th, I shall depart for Edo..."
shigezane:3205.markdown:
There are no cranes here at present; they are most rare—a truly extraordinary and most welcome occurrence. Next month, around the 10th, I intend to depart for Edo. Should you happen to visit here in the meantime, I shall be pleased to serve you tea. I am fully occupied throughout this month. I shall await your arrival from the 5th until the end of the month. With utmost respect.

Furthermore, the magnificent black crane shall be specially presented for your enjoyment. I shall also provide a detailed report from the Wakasa region. That is all.

(Kan'ei 8), intercalary 10th month, 14th day: Masamune's official seal

Ifoshu Guest House

I have received cranes, which are entirely unavailable at this time of year. I am exceptionally delighted by this rarity. Please set your departure for Edo for around the 10th of next month. Should you happen to visit here in the meantime, I shall offer you tea. As I have no free time this month, I shall await you from the 5th of next month onward. With utmost respect.

Furthermore, a magnificent black crane—I shall savor it with great care. I shall report the details from Sasa Wakasa's quarters. That is all.

shigezane:3216.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, January 31, Kan'ei 9. The opening reads: "I am pleased to receive this urgent message. The Chancellor passed away on the night of the 24th. However, as I am safe and sound here, you may rest assured. At any time..."

I hereby send this urgent message of congratulations. The Chancellor passed away on the evening of the 24th. However, as we are all safe and sound, you may rest assured. Should there be any business at any time, please notify us; any prior visit will certainly be unnecessary. Should there be any changes, we shall notify you via courier. With utmost respect. End.

Thank you for your kind letter. The Great Elder, Lord Hidetada, passed away on the evening of the 24th. However, as there are no untoward developments here, please rest assured. Should you have any business, I will let you know at any time; until then, please refrain from visiting the capital. Should any emergency arise, I shall dispatch a courier with instructions. With utmost respect.

shigezane:3220.title: February 24, Kan'ei 9? Letter by Masamune Date
shigezane:3220.summary: February 24, Kan'ei 9? Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Regarding the matter of the marriage arrangement for Jibu-no-daifu, a messenger has been dispatched, and I have given my approval. The daughter of Shirakawa Kunai-no-daifu is entirely suitable. Please proceed with the arrangements promptly..."
shigezane:3220.markdown:
Regarding the marriage arrangement for Jibu-no-Tasuke, a messenger has been dispatched, and I have given him full satisfaction. The daughter of Shirakawa Kunai-no-Tasuke is entirely suitable. It is most appropriate that arrangements be made promptly. Furthermore, a request is to be made from the Wakasa estate. With utmost respect and deference.

I shall report further in due course. Masuji has arrived and has already been presented with the delicacies. Things here and in the Kamigata region are exceptionally peaceful. May you be at ease. I have summoned the Shogun to your presence and conveyed various humble requests. These have not been put in writing. That is all.

(Kan'ei 9?) February 24, Masamune's signature

Lord Awa-no-kami Date

I am pleased that you have gone to the trouble of sending a messenger to the capital regarding Munemi's marriage. It is a fine match with the daughter of Yoshitsuna Shirakawa. I request that the proceedings be expedited. Furthermore, an offer is also coming from Sasa Wakasa. With all due respect.

P.S. You sent two trout, which I have already enjoyed. Both Edo and the capital are in tranquility. Rest assured. Recently, the Shogun summoned me to his side, and I received various gracious instructions—too many to record here.

shigezane:3275.title: Letter from Masamune Date, August 7, Kan'ei 10
shigezane:3275.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, August 7, Kan'ei 10. The opening reads: "Regarding the first hishi-kui: Lord Minbu-no-tasuke arrived before nightfall, and since hishi-kui was struck on the same day, I find it particularly satisfactory, as if I had previously been mindful of it. Two..."
shigezane:3275.markdown:
Regarding the Hatsu-hishi-kui: Lord Minbu-no-tasuke arrived before nightfall, and as the hishi-kui was struck on the same day, I find this to be a particularly auspicious sign, having previously been urged to do so. Both shall be presented to Edo. Of the two, one shall certainly be presented to Kinchu. The other shall be prepared for a meal at the castle, which brings me even greater satisfaction. I shall proceed to Shiroishi today. I await your word thereafter. With utmost respect.

(Kan'ei 10) August 7, Masamune's signature

Lord Awa-no-kami Date

Thank you for the Hatsu-hishi-kui. I received some from Minbu Ishikawa last night as well; they mentioned that the hishi-kui were struck on the same day. This serves as a sign that they had taken great care, and I am particularly—indeed, exceptionally—pleased. Both have been presented to Edo. I am all the more satisfied, thinking that once they reach Edo, one will surely be presented to the Imperial Court, and the other will be used for the castle's cuisine. I plan to go to Shiroishi today. Until next time.

shigezane:3285.summary: February 24, Kan'ei 11? Letter from Masamune Date. The opening reads: "Now then, an unexpected fire has broken out, leaving me with no choice. Are the tea and flower containers safe? Yesterday was the finest weather in Japan, and the Noh performances were excellent and truly precious. Previously..."
shigezane:3285.markdown:
Now then, an unexpected fire has broken out, leaving me with no choice. Are the tea and flower containers safe? Yesterday was the finest weather in Japan, and the Noh performances went splendidly and were truly precious. Had a fire occurred beforehand, it would have been utterly ridiculous, but since this was arranged by your arrangements, it reflects well upon you. I humbly submit this letter. As previously agreed, I shall certainly, most certainly, be there on the 28th. That is all.

(Kan'ei 11?) Mid-spring (February) 24, Masamune's signature

(Edge-twisted seal, top inscription) Ifo-shu, Residence of Masamune

Now then, what a regrettable accidental fire. Were the tea and flower containers safe? Yesterday was the finest weather in Japan, and the Noh performances were all splendid and truly wonderful. It would have been utterly ridiculous if the fire had occurred before the event, but since it happened after it had concluded, it preserves appearances—a blessing in disguise. I offer my deepest and most humble condolences. As per our prior agreement, I shall certainly, most certainly be waiting for you on the 28th.

shigezane:3297.title: Letter from Masamune Date, June 22, Kan'ei 11
shigezane:3297.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, June 22, Kan'ei 11. The opening reads: "I have read the letter dated the 7th of this month today, the 22nd, at the hour of the Horse, in Kyoto. As I am young this year, please be mindful of my wishes. My arrival in the capital has been delayed. Now..."
shigezane:3297.markdown:
I have received the letter dated the 7th of this month and have read it today, the 22nd, at the hour of the Horse, in Kyoto. As I am still young this year, please be mindful of my age. My arrival in the capital was delayed. Once again, I was ordered to lead the way, and furthermore, following various gracious instructions, I departed Edo on the 2nd, stayed in Goshu for three days to rest my people and horses, and arrived in Kyoto on the 19th, the weather being fair. Instructions were issued regarding the bridges and other sweeping duties along the way; for every ten ken of the road, there were two or three people each tasked with hoeing and sweeping; as there were no subsequent complications, I proceeded with peace of mind. I wish that you may remain at ease in all matters. I shall report further auspicious news in due course. With utmost respect and humility. Subsequently, as there were an endless stream of attendants here and there, I write this in haste, using my seal. That is all.

(Kan'ei 11) June 22, Masamune, Black Seal

Lord Iya-no-kami

## Reference: Date Masamune Documents No. 3302, Letter to Shigezane Date

Regarding the dispatch of a messenger from Lord Awa-no-kami, I have herewith presented the enclosed letter. The journey was uneventful, and he arrived in Kyoto on the 19th of last month. I trust he is in good health. As I am currently occupied with endless inspections, I have been unable to attend to this matter. Respectfully submitted.

July 7, Kan'ei 11 — Masamune's Seal

Lord Ijibe Tasuke

shigezane:333.title: Letter from Masamune Date, October 22, Tensho 16
shigezane:333.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, October 22, Tensho 16. The opening reads: "Namely, while this matter was to be addressed via a circular letter, it has been entirely withheld, and thus there is no need for it. It is of utmost importance that the Asaka region and the Tamura district remain peaceful..."
shigezane:333.markdown:
That is to say, while this matter should have warranted a reply, it has been entirely suppressed, and thus no such correspondence has occurred. It is of utmost importance that the Asaka and Ta (Tamura) districts remain peaceful. I intend to dispatch a messenger to Iwaki shortly. Regarding the unusual circumstances at that post, I shall report them. Regarding Mogami, I shall dispatch a messenger starting on the 26th. Furthermore, from Yamagata, Ishiseki Kawachi-no-kami has expressed various earnest requests. He is essentially a close confidant. I trust you will understand. Regarding Shonai, all matters concerning the Honjo side have been transferred. They are firmly established. Starting with Yuri and Senboku, it is understood that their loyalty lies with the Honjo. Regarding Osaki, recently they have been relying entirely on Mogami. As for the discrepancies in Shonai, it is understood that there is also a rift of intent toward Mogami. The situation is pressing and chaotic, leaving no room for error. Now then, the developments and various reports during this spring are inconsistent. Accordingly, we must remain vigilant against the world. Regarding the matter of the South Gate, I shall receive the details shortly. I shall handle it as appropriate. However, should you let your guard down regarding that matter, what would become of it? May good fortune follow. Respectfully and humbly submitted.

Furthermore. Regarding this matter at Takano, I have finally reached a conclusion. As the world will be quiet next spring, I wish to send a hawk to you in concert. That is all.

(Tensho 16) October 22, Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

shigezane:3449.title: Letter from Masamune Date, September 10, Kan'ei era
shigezane:3449.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, dated the 10th day of the 9th month during the Kan'ei era. It begins: "As the gods of Japan also look upon this, I deem it fitting to report the following: salmon have gathered below; upon hearing this, I hastened forth to report it..."
shigezane:3449.markdown:
As the gods of Japan also behold this, I deem it fitting to state that salmon have gathered beneath the river; yet, having spoken so abruptly, I have become flustered and delayed my words. As Minta (Ishikawa Munetaka), Bushu (Date Munetoshi), and Sata (Date Saemon-no-tasuke Shigezane) are of the same mind, I wish to accompany you in private; however, given the rustic setting, I fear it may be difficult to do so. I humbly submit this respectfully.

Please come to Watari tomorrow without delay; that shall be as it should be. The matter is straightforward and simple. Your party is most appropriate. Regarding the matter of Jibu, I have received it with great care. As we are only a short time away from our departure, it would be best to summon you next spring. Again, as we shall likely feel lonely in our absence, it shall be next year. Meanwhile, I have sent seven salmon today. In total, I have received 65. I have dispatched them to various places, so please be advised accordingly. That is all.

September 10, Masamune (kao)

(Twisted-seal cover)

Ifoshu, Guest House, Masamune

※ "As we are about to depart, we are now just a short while away; we shall likely summon you next spring. Again and again, we fear we shall feel lonely in our absence, so we shall do so next year"—could this be the beginning of Munemi's move to Watari? (Takemizu's note)

shigezane:3548.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 4, Tensho 16
shigezane:3548.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 4, Tensho 16. The opening reads: "While I was prepared to respond immediately, matters of a discussion that was difficult to set aside were brought up, causing a delay. Now, word has also reached me here from Koriyama, and—"
shigezane:3548.markdown:
I had intended to respond immediately, but due to a matter of negotiation that proved difficult to set aside, I have allowed the matter to be delayed. Now, word has reached me from Koriyama; I await your report as to the date for the arrangements. As there are numerous idle rumors circulating these days, it is imperative that you carefully note the deadline for settling the matter. Incidentally, I met with the Tamura (Tamura) retainers the day before yesterday. That has been handled accordingly. Having received the general details of the Tamura matter, I have been negotiating from yesterday evening until today, and more than half the matter has been settled. I shall report the details to you in person. With utmost respect.

Furthermore: From Taka (Takatama), I set sail for Yasukojima, crossed over, and slew the enemy. I verified the beach, stone by stone. That is all.

May 4, Year of the Water Rat (Tensho 16), Hour of the Horse. Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

shigezane:3595.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, March 28, Tensho 19. The opening reads: "As this letter finds you well, I write a brief note. I hear that all is proceeding without incident during your absence. In the end, I am most pleased that you remain in good health. Regarding the affairs of the province..."
shigezane:3595.markdown:
This is a brief note regarding your safe journey. Regarding the matter of your continued safety during your absence, each of us has reported it to you. In the end, I am most pleased that you remain in good health. As for the affairs of the province, it has been arranged that they will take place around the beginning of the coming week. However, upon your arrival, I shall immediately proceed to the inner quarters. Please keep this in mind as a precaution. I await your favorable news. Respectfully and humbly.

(Tensho 19) March 28, Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

shigezane:368.title: Letter from Masamune Date, January 24, Tensho 17
shigezane:368.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, January 24, Tensho 17. The opening reads: "I have heard the matter concerning the Tamura retainers. Having felt uneasy after receiving the report the other day, I have now read the letter in detail and find that the Tamura retainers are, first and foremost, entirely at fault..."
shigezane:368.markdown:
Regarding the matter with the Tamura (Tamura) retainers: Having recently received the report, I felt uneasy; however, upon reviewing the correspondence in detail, I find that the Tamura retainers were indeed entirely at fault. For before the issue of Iwaki was resolved, the matter had already reached Ko (Ono) and Dai (Okoshi); thus, in Iwa (Iwaki), it will certainly be recorded that we were unsuccessful. Even if the matter is delayed only slightly, once the resolution of Iwa is confirmed—even if three or four households were to fall into disorder again—it will be unavoidable. Furthermore, regarding the matter of Okoshi, I am well aware of it here as well. Since Ono has the capacity to sustain us through January and February, if matters are handled in Iwaki as if we had been unsuccessful and assistance is provided to Ono, would that not be for the benefit of Tamura and ourselves? Today, the 24th, a courier is planned to be dispatched from Tamura (Tamura). First, I shall convey these sentiments. However, I am prepared to further report the details to Tamura (Tamura) with full clarity. Meanwhile, I ask for your discernment and consultation through this channel at a later date. With utmost respect and humility.

Furthermore, during my brief illness, my wording and other matters may have been improper. That is all.

(Tensho 17) January 24, Hour of the Rooster — Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

## See letter to Kojuro Katakura dated the same day (original text primarily in kana)

It is fitting that you consult with the Tamura retainers. I hear the details thoroughly, and for now, I have no basis for judgment. However, should you fail to heed Iwaki's hidden intentions and sever ties with Ono and Okoshi, Iwaki may treat our side unfavorably; thus, even if matters are delayed slightly, it is best to proceed as is. Should the matter be abruptly terminated, Iwaki will surely harbor resentment toward us and seek retribution through Ono; therefore, for now, one should exercise restraint. That said, should there be any unusual discretion, I shall report it from here on. Furthermore, while this letter is being prepared, I shall send a reply with heartfelt greetings regarding the letter from Yakatagaoka, despite it being a New Year's greeting. In any case, it is fitting to reply with something somewhat unusual. I shall continue in this manner and remain at your service. Best regards. Respectfully.

This letter shall be kept safe and guarded. Firmly and securely.

(Tensho 17) January 24, Hour of the Rooster, Official Seal

Katako

shigezane:3752.title: Letter from Masamune Date, October 4, Kan'ei era
shigezane:3752.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, dated the 4th day of the 10th month during the Kan'ei era. It begins: "In the vicinity of Kasajima in Natori, there are six or seven cranes. Although I have used hawks to※ them, they are too old and have proven ineffective. I have driven them away, hoping to find a suitable place..."
shigezane:3752.markdown:
In the vicinity of Natori Kasajima, there are six or seven cranes. Though I have used hawks, they are too old to be of any use. I have driven them about, hoping to drive them to a suitable spot, but they will not leave their perch. I intend to have them shot with firearms. There are skilled marksmen here as well, but I have ordered them to shoot the cranes. [Kayaba Genbei](#/post/shigezane/kasin) is to come here tomorrow before dawn. If so, I shall have one guide wait at Iwanuma. It is only fitting that the man be shot accordingly. With all due respect.

For two days starting from the first day, I sent out hawks; yesterday, I ventured out to Tano-takano and had three hawks from the bird-keeper's stable stationed there; I replaced them one by one with tubes, and I am fully satisfied. Respectfully.

October 4, Masamune (kao)

Ifoshu Goshukujo

shigezane:393.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, March 19, Tensho 17. The opening reads: "While I ought to state my thoughts from hereon, I am delighted to receive this brief note. Furthermore, it is a great joy that the matter regarding Kata (Katahira) has been settled. Additionally, Kojuro..."

(Tensho 17) 19th day of the third month, Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

shigezane:395.title: Letter from Masamune Date, March 21, Tensho 17
shigezane:395.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, March 21, Tensho 17. The opening reads: "While matters are pending, I send this letter in a single document. Now, regarding the matter of opening the passage at Tamura Kamimata (Shikamata), if the matter is delayed, as to how various matters will proceed, there are no objections, starting with the Asaka entrance..."
shigezane:395.markdown:
While the matter is pending, I hereby send a single note. Regarding the matter of the passage through Tamura Kamimata (Kamamata), if the proceedings are delayed and questions arise as to how various matters should be handled—since there has been no objection thus far regarding the Asaka entrance—I intend to arrange this; therefore, following consultations among the Tamura (Tamura) retainers, it should be settled shortly. As for the matters currently stalled in Tamura (Tamura), I have instructed Kata-ko (Kojuro Katakura) with the details; since I have issued instructions to both Date Higashine and Nishine, it is crucial that these be forwarded to Tamura (Tamura) to ensure the passage is secured. However, regarding the matter of salt, I shall receive further instructions. As this is a matter of utmost urgency, please act swiftly. With utmost respect and deference.

Further note. Regarding the matter of the passage, how should it be handled that the two of you be forwarded to Tamura (Tamura)? As the matter of Katahira is naturally difficult to resolve, I believe Shigezane should remain in Fujiyama (Nihonmatsu). I have instructed Kata-ko (Kojuro Katakura) with the details. That is all.

(Tensho 17) March 21, Hour of the Snake, Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro

Hakuu (Munemi Shiroishi)

shigezane:427.title: Letter from Masamune Date, May 14, Tensho 17
shigezane:427.summary: Letter from Masamune Date, May 14, Tensho 17. The opening reads: "Having received reports regarding your arrival in accordance with both channels, I believe that deliberations concerning the Tamura (Tamura) boundary will inevitably take place; therefore, it would be appropriate to proceed promptly to the Tamura (Tamura) area. Respectfully..."
shigezane:427.markdown:
Having received reports via both channels regarding their arrival, I believe there will certainly be deliberations concerning the Ta (Tamura) border; therefore, it would be appropriate to proceed swiftly to the Ta (Tamura) area. The situation is utterly uncontrollable. Furthermore, word has reached us from Koriyama that they are coming this way. It is said that Yoshishige (Satake) is launching an offensive. This morning, merchants descended from Sukagawa. These individuals visit Yonezawa every year. In their idle conversation, they mentioned that there is not the slightest inkling that Yoshishige will launch an offensive. Let us remain vigilant. Additionally, it is said that they are coming to Katahira to inquire about the situation. First, I believe it would be appropriate to proceed to the Ta (Tamura) tomorrow. With utmost respect and deference.

Furthermore, regarding the matter of Inawa (Inawashiro), the verse also does not flow smoothly. I find this unsettling.

(Tensho 17) May 14, Hour of the Dog; Masamune (kao)

Lord Goro
