shigezane:masamuneki4-4.title: The matter settled between Ouchi Bizen and Masamune
shigezane:masamuneki4-4.summary: On March 23 of the same year, after the auction at Tamanoi had concluded and Shigezane returned to Nihonmatsu, Ouchi Bizen and Katahira Sukeemon—who had been arranged by the parties involved—headed to Nihonmatsu, waiting to accompany Date.
shigezane:masamuneki4-4.markdown:
On March 23 of the same year, after a skirmish at Tamanoi, Shigezane returned to Nihonmatsu. Ouchi Bizen and Katahira Sukeemon, who had been arranged by the parties involved, set out for Nihonmatsu, waiting to proceed to Date. Meanwhile, on the night of April 5, a man named Kajiuchi Danjo—a nephew of Bizen—came to Kagetsuna's lodgings and said, "Ouchi has departed for my lord's residence tonight, and Sukeemon is also scheduled to commit seppuku tomorrow; I have already gone ahead." Accordingly, Shigezane also proceeded to my lord's residence along with Kagetsuna, and upon meeting Bizen on the 6th, he stated, "While we had firmly agreed upon the matter of Sukeemon's seppuku, there were slight discrepancies, and a dispute arose between the brothers; it seemed certain that I were to be killed, so I have reluctantly withdrawn." Upon hearing this, Kagetsuna and Shigezane spoke of their brothers, saying, "Now, as Sukeemon had stated above that nothing was amiss, Bizen claimed Sukeemon was likewise without fault; that is precisely why the discrepancy now appears. In any case, if Ouchi goes to Date, will Sukeemon ultimately remain loyal to us? If not, suspicion will arise from Aizu and Katahira will be replaced; in any event, the end will not be peaceful—their judgment was mistaken." Despite this, as Ouchi had already departed and no force was present, fearing how the news would reach Aizu, Shiroishi Wakasa, Kagetsuna, and Shigezane—three men—went to Akugashima. However, they encountered not a single enemy cavalryman, nor did the party have any means of engaging them; they withdrew that day and attempted another operation the following day. Ishikawa Danjo, stationed at Yonhon-no-Matsu, turned against Date and sided with Soma; he committed seppuku within the Wakasa territory at Yonhon-no-Matsu and set fire to the area. Consequently, Wakasa withdrew midway through the operation. Only Kagetsuna and Shigezane continued the operation, but they withdrew without incident; Kagetsuna returned to Omori, the castle of Shinobu, on April 9. Afterward, he requested an audience with Bizen Masamune, stating his intentions. His younger brother Sukeemon, fearing he might lack loyalty, replied, "Moreover, if the spearhead of your lord were to strike, Bizen would surrender and submit to the house; furthermore, the reputation of the neighboring provinces—Aizu, Satake, and Iwaki—would be beyond measure." Masamune accepted this and dispatched Shigezane and his retainers, accompanied by Endo Suruga, to Yonezawa for the audience. This occurred when Masamune was twenty-two years old.

shigezane:masamuneki4-5.title: Regarding Ishikawa Danjo's Entry
shigezane:masamuneki4-5.summary: On April 12 of the same year, Ishikawa Danjo also entered a place called Nishi in the Wakasa territory; he himself also ventured out, and struck down two people who had emerged from within early in the morning. Upon learning this within the castle, he drove those who had emerged back into the castle and launched an attack from there...
shigezane:masamuneki4-5.markdown:
On the twelfth day of the fourth month of the same year, Ishikawa Danjo also entered a place called Nishi in the Wakasa territory and ventured out himself; he slew one or two men who had emerged from within early in the morning. Upon learning this within the castle, he drove those who had emerged back into the castle and launched an attack. The sound of muskets was frequently heard in Obama, and as Wakasa was quickly summoned, Danjo withdrew upon seeing them; Wakasa then seized the opportunity and engaged them, achieving victory and taking twenty or thirty heads. Shigezane also heard the sound of muskets at Nihonmatsu and quickly gathered his forces, but as the distance was great, separated by the Abukuma River, he arrived late and failed to coordinate his plans; however, Wakasa was delighted by his arrival and summoned him to Miyamori, treating him with an exceptional feast. Now, Danjo was originally a retainer of Kyukichi, the lord of Yonbonmatsu, and had been longtime rivals with Ouchi Bizen. However, because Kyukichi's conduct had long been poor, the entire retainer corps rose up and each took his own stand to denounce Kyukichi. From there, Danjo—his own father, Settsu-no-kami—approached Tamura Kiyoaki, while Ouchi served the Date. When the Date father and son were in turmoil due to Nakano's treason, the later Bizen Sadatsuna also relied on Tamura, serving him as a neighbor; however, due to disputes between the two retainers mentioned above, Tamura Uma-no-kami and Katahira Sukeemon, the latter harbored resentment toward Ouchi Kiyoaki and remained hostile for several years. Nevertheless, Danjo's position remained unchanged, and he served as the magistrate for Tamura. Subsequently, when Masamune took possession of the residence at Yonbonmatsu, all of Danjo's holdings were also within Yonbonmatsu. Eventually, Kiyoaki handed Tamura over to Masamune, promising that if a daughter were born, she would be entrusted to Lord Tamura. Therefore, Kiyoaki told Danjo, "Not for your own sake, but for the sake of the holdings, serve Masamune," and he entered his service. In addition, four or five others, including Terasakayama-jo and Ouchi Noto, as well as those from Kyukichi's retainer corps who now served Tamura, were all placed under Masamune's command. Accordingly, when Masamune declared that Danjo was a fellow retainer of Wakasa, he directly appointed him, granting him not only his original lands but even additional increases. Nevertheless, because he had previously been an enemy of Masamune, he cherished his own well-being above all else. Furthermore, as Masamune's relationship with his wife was poor at the time, his mother-in-law held a grudge against him; while Danjo was fully aware of her conspiracies with Soma Yoshitane, she betrayed the Date and leaned toward Soma. From the twelfth day of the fourth month of Tensho 16, she severed ties with him, and from then on, she continued to betray the Date.

shigezane:masamuneki4-6.title: Operations from Aizu
shigezane:masamuneki4-6.summary: On the night of April 5 of the same year, news reached Aizu of the surrender of Ouchi, Bizen, and Date; the men of Aizu convened at Sukagawa, and word arrived that they were launching an attack on the Asaka front.
shigezane:masamuneki4-6.markdown:
On the night of April 5th, word reached Aizu regarding the surrender of Ouchi, Bizen, and Date. The forces of Aizu coordinated with Sukagawa and were preparing to strike out toward the Asaka front. When Kagetsuna Katakura was notified of this, he immediately departed his castle and arrived at Nihonmatsu to alert the forces of Shinobu. However, as the news came so suddenly, not a single person joined him. With only Kagetsuna and Shigezane's forces, and without having even secured their equipment, they hurriedly rushed toward Motomiya. They attempted to secure Takakura as well, but as there were no troops present at the time, Shigezane managed to gather just over twenty cavalrymen and fifty muskets from the residents of his eighth-chome territory. Consequently, the forces from Takakura and Omi also arrived at Motomiya on the 17th. These Omi troops were hereditary retainers of Nihonmatsu and were well-acquainted with the routes to Aizu and Asaka. When asked, "Where will the enemy operate tomorrow, and how many troops will they have?" they replied, "The garrisons at the border between Aizu and Sukagawa have not slackened their vigilance; combined, the two locations likely exceed a thousand cavalrymen. Furthermore, their operations tomorrow will surely push through to Motomiya, and likely as far as Takakura." Upon hearing this, Kagetsuna and Shigezane agreed: "In that case, tomorrow we shall follow the enemy's movements; you shall strike out toward the Kannon-do and provide reinforcements to Takakura. That said, it depends on how things unfold. If they advance toward Motomiya and you do not withdraw inside, the enemy will surely be prepared at the Kannon-do. If they withdraw further down, that would be even more desirable. Even if it is beyond our expectations, we shall deploy our men, attack from this side to drive the enemy back to the town entrance, and begin a skirmish. Shigezane and his men shall have Haneda Uma-no-suke take the lead, with Kagetsuna following. Shigezane shall not engage in the fighting itself, but shall push his forces to the west side toward the Kannon-do; if the enemy's footsteps are disrupted, we shall strike from Takakura tomorrow." They then returned Omi to Takakura. On the 18th, at the hour of the Rabbit, distant fire was launched toward the west of the castle. Believing this to be an attack on Takakura, they deployed troops beneath the Kannon-do, who in turn advanced eastward. As it appeared they were heading toward Motomiya, they intended to withdraw the forces that had advanced, following their prior agreement. However, since troops had already moved out and it would be too late to recall them that day, they decided to maintain their defense. Kagetsuna and Shigezane took their positions at the Kannon-do and gave the signal for battle. The enemy advanced in stages. Among them, Kanokoda Uemon charged alone, riding through with forty or fifty ashigaru. Shigezane and his men instructed Ishikawa Yahei: "You shall lead the charge, draw Kanokoda toward us, and advance steadily. If you continue to advance upon this, we shall engage in battle. Move out quickly." Haneda Uma-no-suke brought along over thirty ashigaru; Yahei advanced and exchanged fire, gradually breaking through the boundary between friend and foe, drawing Kanokoda out and bringing him back toward them. This display was truly a spectacle of a battlefield, beyond description. Uemon was initially alone, but later arrived with over ten cavalrymen and over a hundred ashigaru. When Kagetsuna and Shigezane forced them back beneath the Kannon-do, Uma-no-suke and Yahei pursued them as far as the Kannon-do. Once they released their hold, the enemy collapsed as expected. Uma-no-suke charged at a man named Bunkuro, who was sixteen years old; he thrust at a suited warrior, overturned him, and cut down Bunkuro. He then engaged three or four foot soldiers, intending to take their heads, but Uma-no-suke charged in and pinned two of them down; since one took the head, the enemy was repelled, and Bunkuro's head could not be taken. Consequently, the forces crossing from Hitotori Bridge fled across the bridge in formation, avoiding the defenses. Meanwhile, the enemy repositioned themselves opposite the bridge, and the allies were repelled. Kangoro Maetaka, a page to Masamune, had been incensed and was stationed at the defenses relying on Shigezane. As he charged and drove the enemy back, he struck the horse's great stride, throwing his spear and striking the shoulder of the enemy, who then fell. Kangoro stood up, cast off his armor and entrusted it to a servant, took up a hand spear, charged at a single suited warrior, and struck him down. He earned great renown for taking the head and presented it to Shigezane. When Masamune was informed of this, he said it was unparalleled and forgave him; Kangoro was granted a reward for his achievement. Meanwhile, the allied troops were pursued back to the Kannon-do, but Haneda Uma-no-suke, Ushizaka Sakon, and Ishikawa Yahei fought back and drove the enemy away, pursuing them as far as Hitotori Bridge. They slew fifty-six miscellaneous soldiers, while fourteen of their own were killed; they celebrated the victory separately. On the 17th, the distant fire agreed upon had been fired; had there been a discrepancy in the timing, many would likely have been slain, but because the timing was precise, the victory was decided by a small margin. Later, when asked about the discrepancy in the signal fire, they replied, "We went west first so that we could learn of today's operations." The enemy replied, "We knew of your operations from yesterday, which is why we coordinated our plan; you acted on your own." However, it was of no use. The Aizu forces, having completed their operation, returned to camp, taking the elderly mother of Katahirasuke Uemon as a witness. In general, although they had come from Aizu to take hostages, they feared that if no action were taken, word would spread in all directions; thus, they proceeded as described above. Kagetsuna remained stationed at Motomiya until the 21st of the same month, but upon hearing that the enemy had returned to camp, he departed for Yonezawa on the 23rd.

shigezane:masamuneki4-7html.title: The Lawsuit of the Tamura Elders
shigezane:masamuneki4-7html.summary: In the same fourth month, due to the treachery of Ishikawa Danjo, those inclined toward Soma and those defending Date were gathered at Tamura, intending for Masamune to march out without delay; however, as nothing of the sort occurred, it was only natural that everyone grew suspicious.
shigezane:masamuneki4-7html.markdown:
In the fourth month of the same year, due to the treason of Ishikawa Danjo, those inclined toward Soma and those defending Date were gathering at Tamura, intending for Masamune to march out without delay. However, as nothing of the sort occurred, it was only natural that everyone grew suspicious. Nevertheless, Masamune himself likely had his reasons; although Mogami Yoshiaki of the neighboring province was Masamune's uncle, he was a greedy general who knew nothing of his son's inner intentions and desired the castle of Yonezawa. As he had employed various stratagems through Ayugai Totaro, as mentioned previously, it would have been impossible for him to have marched out without prior notice. At that time, Tamura Gessai, Hashimoto Gyobu, and Shiroishi Wakasa approached him and said, "Ishikawa Danjo has acted with treason; while people expected him to lead out his horses to subdue him, he has not done so. Furthermore, while Tamura is half inclined toward Soma, it still fears the sharp edge of his spear and has not yet taken action. To bring Yoshitane forward this time, Danjo has turned against Date; thus, unless he leads out his horses, it cannot be achieved." Masamune replied, "Though it is said one should march out without delay, in the current war with Mogami, I have stationed high-ranking officials at every boundary; however, the Mogami border is occupied by low-ranking men. Therefore, my hesitation is that I should not march out from Yonezawa. Moreover, if I were to lead out my horses, I might subdue them or fail to capture a single location, and in just a day or two's campaign, it would surely become known to all directions. Thus, if I am to subdue them, I must allow several days to pass; otherwise, it would be unwise to march out from the castle indefinitely." Gessai and Gyobu replied again, "If the people of Tamura, unaware of your true intentions, believe you have no intention of leading out your horses, they will all lean toward Soma. Furthermore, not only your own house but the generals of other provinces are undoubtedly skilled in their craft. Even if it is not for an extended stay, if they make a single campaign, there will surely be some gain. The peace of Tamura until now is only because it feared your departure; now that nothing of the sort occurs, there is no doubt that those men will be killed." Therefore, Masamune said, "The arguments of these two are sufficient. I shall deliberate upon it," and ordered the army to mobilize. On the 29th of the fourth month, he departed from Yonezawa; on the 30th, he led his horses to Omori in Shinobu, stayed there for three days, and on May 4th, he moved to the fortified residence at Yone-bon-no-Matsu. The residence of Danjo was a place called Gassan, and Kode-no-Mori was a place called Yone-bon-no-Matsu, which he acquired at that time; furthermore, there was a residence called Hyakume-gi, belonging to Danjo's father, Settsu-no-kami, which was on the border of Soma. Meanwhile, as attacks were expected from the vicinity of the fortified residence, he first led out to Kode-no-Mori, but as attacks were also launched toward Gassan, he struck a blow one day before Yoshitane, seizing Gassan, and left Danjo entrenched at Kode-no-Mori. Thus, Masamune, wishing to see the terrain of Kode-no-Mori, passed from north to south; although muskets were fired from within, he remained unconcerned and withdrew without incident on a certain day. As for Shigezane, he remained concerned about the southern route and returned to Nihonmatsu that night. The next day it rained, but since Shigezane also came to the fortified residence, the operations ceased. From then on, he visited daily, but as the weather was poor and operations were impossible, on May 7th, Masamune also withdrew to Omori. Gessai and Gyobu were surprised by this withdrawal and, through Shiroishi Wakasa and Shigezane, said, "We spoke of a campaign, but since you were to march out, we thought you would campaign for four or five days. Although we understand it was due to the weather, withdrawing after only one day's campaign suggests that you care deeply for the Mogami border; if the people of Tamura believe this, those defending Date may change their allegiance. If things do not work out in either Yonezawa or Tamura, you would soon be attacked from all sides; how should it be that people believe you are staying at Omori?" Thus, Wakasa and Shigezane went to Omori and explained the matter to Harada Kyusetsu, Moriya Morikashi, Ito Hizen, and Katakura Kagetsuna. Hizen said, "Your argument is sound, but as you know, not a single high-ranking official is stationed in Yonezawa, while the Mogami border is occupied by low-ranking men. Even if you speak of a swift attack, the distance from here to that border is two hundred ri of country roads; whatever they claim, it will likely be nothing." Wakasa said, "Furthermore, they think of Tamura as merely a large entity. It is because Gessai and Gyobu are so devoted to their service and have pressed Tamura that things have remained peaceful until now. If you withdraw to Omori, those two will lose trust and change their allegiance; the situation is grave." Hizen added, "Even if they change their allegiance, it is of no use if mischief arises in Yonezawa; for now, you should manage the affairs of the castle well and keep Tamura under control." Kagetsuna said, "There is no room for debate here; I shall present this to you and follow your orders." As they each presented the matters, Masamune said, "Withdrawing because the rain continued and no progress was made is contrary to my intent. As you both wish, let the men and horses rest here; if things do not work out in either direction, rest assured that I shall strike swiftly." When Wakasa's side conveyed this, Gessai and Gyobu were not displeased. Thereafter, while staying at Omori, he set out on May 11th to inspect the area around Takakura in Asaka District. Upon hearing that Shigezane was passing through, he departed from his residence at Nihonmatsu and pursued him at Motomiya, accompanying him as far as the place called Maeda-zawa-hori, and returned to Omori that day. Meanwhile, as there were various rumors among the commoners in Tamura, Gessai, Gyobu, and Kagetsuna conspired and secretly inquired, reporting: "Lord Masamune is encamped at Omori, and Lord Yoshitane is encamped at Gassan. If either side sends people into Tamura to commit mischief, it cannot be helped. Even if they say they have business, from now on, I believe the Date forces will naturally be involved, and the Soma forces as well. But what do you all think?" Upon this, Umeyuki, Uemon, and the other leaders all agreed. Thus, Gessai, Gyobu, and Kagetsuna agreed upon this, and from then on, they ceased all communication.

shigezane:masamuneki4-8html.title: Regarding Yoshitane's Loss of the Tamura Domain
shigezane:masamuneki4-8html.summary: In the same May, while Masamune resided at Omori and Yoshitane at Gassan, Masamune continued to align himself with Yoshitane, a retainer of Tamura; meanwhile, Masamune's aunt, who resided at Miharu Castle, was Yoshitane's aunt, but at that time she harbored resentment toward Masamune and leaned toward Soma...
shigezane:masamuneki4-8html.markdown:
In the same month of May, while Masamune was stationed at Omori and Yoshitane was at Gassan, Masamune continued to align himself with Yoshitane, a retainer of Tamura. Meanwhile, Masamune's aunt, who resided at Miharu Castle, harbored resentment toward him and was leaning toward Soma; she was conspiring to have Tamura seized by Yoshitane. Accordingly, on the 11th, Soma dispatched two envoys—Yamashiro and Nakamura Sukeemon—to inform Yoshitane at Miharu, stating, "It is a fortunate thing that you are currently encamped at nearby Gassan; we shall visit you there tomorrow to pay our respects." Consequently, the lower retainers of Tamura declared, "We had previously made a firm pact that neither Date nor Soma would enter; now that the situation has changed and two envoys have arrived, if Yoshitane is present tomorrow, it would be a means to seize the castle." Thus, at the hour of the Tiger on the 12th, Yamashiro and Sukeemon ascended from their respective lodgings in Miharu to Miharu Castle, where they awaited Yoshitane. At that time, Hashimoto Gyobu, prepared to commit suicide, entered the castle during the night; it is said that five men from Gyobu's side, three each, entered the fortress armed with bows, muskets, and armor. As Gessai, Baisetsu, and Uemon also arrived, Gyobu took the hand of Baisetsu and said, "Let us reverse our previous agreement and have you enter now." Baisetsu had privately discussed that if Gyobu were to depart for Tamura, he should be allowed to take him along; however, Gyobu likely thought that if the response were unfavorable, he should strike him down immediately. Against all expectations, Gyobu replied, "No, I shall not enter." Taking the bow, Gyobu slung his armor over his shoulders and fired his musket, creating a chaotic melee. As they fought with their respective equipment, Yoshitane had already ascended to the middle of the slope; a musket shot struck the horse's neck, and though he turned back and circled toward the eastern flank, he found the position critical. The accompanying soldiers—over thirty cavalrymen in hakama—were of no use and retreated in vain. Meanwhile, over two hundred armored warriors, equipped with bows, spears, and muskets, had waited in ambush, timing their arrival to follow from behind; however, as the engagement had already taken place, they did not encounter them. Furthermore, Okoshi Kii-no-kami had also conspired, hiding his forces in a deep valley within the castle woods since evening, but due to the general's lack of skill, he failed to be of use and returned to Gassan. Kii-no-kami went to meet him along the way and said, "Please stop by," but Okoshi did not stop and headed straight for Soma. Yamashiro and Sukeemon, thinking they should strike within the castle, grew increasingly anxious over Yoshitane's departure. Deciding that it would be futile, they stepped out, but as everyone thrust their spears forward, Gyobu gave the order that it was useless. He instructed Yamashiro and Sukeemon, "Since the situation at the fortress is thus, please prepare yourselves and, keeping this in mind, hurry and inform Yoshitane," then pushed forward and held the castle firmly. Meanwhile, Yamashiro and Sukeemon, hearing Gyobu's words, grew impatient and, in a panic, thought to storm the gates. They emerged quietly as far as outside the gates, but Yamashiro said to the gatekeeper, "With such precautions in place, how can you simply break the chains?" The gatekeeper, realizing the intent, fastened the locks. Hearing this, the two hurriedly fled and descended, pursuing Yoshitane to Soma. The people of the time whispered that these were pitiful yet brave men who, having saved their own lives, had cast aside their loyalty to their lord and lost their eyesight. Consequently, on that day, the aforementioned items were sent from Tamura to Obama, and Shiroishi Wakasa sent a messenger to Omori at the hour of the Boar that night; Masamune wasted no time and gathered his forces. On the 13th, at the hour of the Dragon, he arrived at the Four-Pine Shrine Forest. From there, he led Date Nobuo's troops to attack Gassan over two days, declaring that troops would enter Tamura, and sent Shigezane to a place within Tamura called Shiraiwa. However, Shigezane did not appear during the two days of attack. On the 16th, he attacked Kote-no-mori; on that day, he summoned Shigezane, stationed reinforcements from Gassan, and launched a general assault, causing the castle to fall and signal fires. This time, he did not execute the prisoners but ordered them to be dispersed, and he returned to Mimori. On the 17th, Hikoshichiro, the lord of a place called Okura, was the younger brother of Tamura Uemon; among the kinsmen of Tamura who had shifted their allegiance to Date, not to mention those who had not yet been executed, Hikoshichiro had remained inconspicuous, appearing only occasionally while Yoshitane was encamped at Gassan. When Yoshitane moved to Miharu, Hikoshichiro acted first and opposed Masamune. Consequently, Hikoshichiro pressed the attack upon the Okura castle fortifications, but they retreated into the fortress. Though the houses were burned down, not a single cavalryman emerged, and no reinforcements came from the flanks. At that point, Hikoshichiro—perhaps per the previous agreement, or perhaps because his brother Uemon had arranged it—sent Baisetsu, a monk, to the place called Tosetsu to file a lawsuit. Masamune accepted the challenge, but as the sun set, he first retreated to Mimori. Thus, all the troops set up camp in a place called Nishi. On the 18th, hearing that Soma forces had gathered at Ishizawa in Tamura, he dispatched horses to attack that location. However, as Hikoshichiro refused to surrender, all the troops took up positions on the road to Okura, resolving that if they did not emerge, they would attack this fortress; thus, everyone prepared themselves and immediately surrendered, and it was decided that they would lead the advance to Ishizawa. Ishizawa was a small place but a fortress; hearing that many Soma forces had joined them, they deliberated whether to press the attack or maintain a close position. That night, they decided to spend the night at a place called Nishi in the domain of Shiroishi Wakasa, but as there were no houses to settle in, they set up camp in the eastern mountains. Then, a great thunderbolt struck, causing hardship for everyone. At that time, fires were seen at Gassan; though it was thunder, scouts were sent, and upon returning, they reported, "The enemy at Gassan has retreated without a single person remaining." When asked, "And what of Ishizawa?" it was said that not only that place, but even the castle of Danjo Chika Settsu-no-kami at Hyakumoki had been cleared; as the Soma forces within Tamura were leaning toward Soma, three points were captured at the front, and they returned to Mimori to rest their horses and men. Thus, Gessai, Baisetsu, Uemon, Gyobu, and those who had leaned toward Soma all went to Mimori to subdue Ishikawa Danjo; thus, Tamura was granted peace and prosperity, and celebrations were held. During this time, Tokiwa and Iga visited; during the council at Tamura, Tokiwa volunteered to protect Date, and upon hearing that this was the case, he was granted a sword with a gold noshi-wrap. This was when Masamune was twenty-two years old.

## Commentary on Musui

Cross-referencing with the Tensho Diary, the Jike Records, and other sources, the "May" mentioned above is believed to be the "intercalary May."

shigezane:masamuneki4-9html.title: The Lawsuit Concerning the Subjugation of Okoshi
shigezane:masamuneki4-9html.markdown:
And so. Gessai, Baisetsu, Uemon, and Gyobu came to Miyamori and reported to Harada Kyusetsu, Ito Hizen, and Kagetsuna Katakura, saying, "Okoshi Kii-no-kami has not appeared in Sanshun since the beginning; now that Yoshitane intends to take Sanshun, the means to do so are due to the rebellion of that man alone, and he has retreated to the castle. If this is not subdued, what will become of the punishment for Tamura?" Masamune declared, "Kii-no-kami's proposal is sound. Nevertheless, there are reasons why it cannot be realized as hoped. I have heard recently that Satake has departed for the Asaka front. However, if he presses toward Okoshi—perhaps he will be delayed there—and in the meantime Yoshishige marches out, he may bypass the castle and head for the Asaka front; given the enemy's intentions, I shall exercise caution here." The four men replied, "If that is the case, although you have no immediate forces, we must certainly undertake some action." He declared, "Then this time, let the magistrates act." At that moment, Shigezane was encamped at Motomiya; he was summoned to Miyamori and told, "The four men of Tamura are engaged in such a dispute, but given the aforementioned caution, you shall personally go to Okoshi." Shigezane asked, "Regarding Yoshishige's march, there was no word of it at Asaka; from where did you hear of this?" To this, Masamune replied, "The person before you was removed, and in secret, he said, 'Suda Mino-no-kami of Sukagawa knows.'" Shigezane replied, "This is beyond my expectations. I have heard that Mino serves Satake without fail; it is a great pleasure that there is now a connection toward this side as well." Masamune declared, "Since I have sent people to Mino's side twice, I told them that the first messenger was merely a courtesy, and that if there were further business, it should be handled through this channel; yet they did not even notify me of Yoshishige's march. Furthermore, when Ishikawa Yamato Akimitsu sent a mountain ascetic named Yashiro as a courier, there was no word of it; upon inquiring of that ascetic, he stated that Yoshishige's march was certain." And so, he returned to Nihonmatsu, made preparations over two days, and set out from the place called Tamura no Funabiki. From there, he advanced toward Okoshi, but as the defenders had withdrawn and fortified two or three baileys so strongly that there was no way to attack, he withdrew that day. Meanwhile, Masamune had also hidden and marched unnoticed; the forces of Ono and Shikamata attacked from the east, and the Date forces attacked from the north and withdrew. Later, the enemy advanced against the Shikamata group and engaged in battle; as the sounds of muskets rang frequently, Masamune and his entire force counterattacked, breaking the enemy lines and scattering them in all directions, taking over thirty heads. He returned to Miyamori the following day and withdrew the same forces.

An auspicious day in the sixth month of Kan'ei 13 (Year of the Fire Rat) — Shigezane Date of Awa

shigezane:masamuneki9-3.title: Regarding the Establishment of Mukojima
shigezane:masamuneki9-3.summary: From the second month of the first year of Keicho (the year of the Fire Monkey), Taiko Hideyoshi constructed a castle at Mukojima in Fushimi, spanning a bridge from the main castle to establish it as a place of leisure; with the construction more than halfway complete, around midnight on the twelfth day of the intercalary seventh month, a massive earthquake struck, shaking down the castle keep and the palace buildings...
shigezane:masamuneki9-3.markdown:
From the second month of the first year of Keicho (the year of the Fire Monkey), Taiko Hideyoshi constructed a castle at Mukojima in Fushimi, building a bridge from the main castle to facilitate travel and designating it as a place of leisure. Just as more than half of the construction had been completed, around midnight on the twelfth day of the intercalary seventh month, a violent earthquake struck, shaking down the castle keep and the palaces; over fifty men and women within the castle were crushed to death in their homes. Overall, as this island was situated along the Uji River and had a depressed terrain, many stone walls and construction huts collapsed. Nevertheless, perhaps believing that even if the island were rebuilt, it would not be the same, on the twentieth day of the same seventh month, he selected Mount Kohata as the site for the castle. Not to mention the various daimyo, everyone from the hatamoto to the low-ranking retainers, menial servants, and attendants was organized into groups to haul large stones and quarry the terrain; as the imperial decree stated that the construction—including the various palaces—was to be completed by the last day of the twelfth month, they worked urgently, day and night. Stating that nothing could be more perilous than an earthquake, he ordered that two pillars of the palace be sunk to the foundation and the third be driven in to a depth of over five shaku, and that the furnishings above be secured with pegs in various places; thus, contrary to the construction work of previous days, this time the focus was entirely on precautions against earthquakes. Because the construction was rushed, he paid out imperial rewards to those who performed duties with exceptional courage beyond his expectations, and they were all deeply humbled. In October, as the cold began to set in and became severe, he ordered that paper-covered cloths be provided to block the wind; he carried these in long chests and toured the town, distributing them to the various daimyo. Among them, as Masamune was said to be extremely fond of fine arts, he was granted various items: a navy-blue gold brocade collar, dyed sleeves with brushed gold leaf, and a blue satin hem. There were also those who received textiles. Around that time, when Masamune had the boats for transport to and from Osaka prepared, Hideyoshi, moved by his kindness, granted him a sword belonging to Mitsutada. The next day, when Lord Hideyoshi visited the construction site, Masamune wore that sword and presented it before his office; the lord then commanded, "Yesterday, a sword was stolen from Masamune; retrieve it!" Four or five pages rushed forward to seize it, but Masamune drove them back and escaped over ten ken, saying, "Though they are thieves, they are pardoned; come here." There were various such humble imperial rewards. At another time, he brought imperial persimmons in a tray and distributed them among the daimyo; saying, "Since Masamune is fond of fine arts, he likely desires a larger one," he took the contents back from the tray and declared, "There is none larger than this," and received them. The daimyo of the nearby offices, seeing this, spread the rumor: "Though he is a man from a distant province who has served for only four or five years, he is a most devoted and benevolent person, surpassing even those of previous generations."

Plenty of materials regarding the Tamura clan of the Sengoku period. ☆ [Tome History Museum](http://www.city.tome.miyagi.jp/rekihaku/) The castle town of the Sanuma-Watari clan. You can see the personal effects of Ko-no-mae. ☆ [Shirakawa Shuko-en](http://www.shirakawa.ne.jp/~rekimin/) Features transcriptions of documents from the Shirakawa Yuki family. ☆ [Sendai City Museum](http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/museum/) No need for an explanation... incredibly useful. ☆ [Michinoku Date Masamune History Museum](http://www.date-masamune.jp/) A museum where you can see the life of Masamune through wax figures. ☆ [Miyagi Prefecture Keicho Embassy Ship Museum](http://www.santjuan.or.jp/) A reconstruction of the Bautista. ☆ [Date City Funkawan Cultural Research Institute](http://www.funkawan.net/index.html) Houses documents from the Watari Date family. ☆ [Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Perspective](http://mogamiyoshiaki.jp/index.php) Apparently, if Masamune is a dragon, Yoshiaki is a tiger. No matter how you look at it, it's all about Mogami Yoshiaki. I want to go! ☆ [Cultural Properties of Ishikawa Town](http://www.town.ishikawa.fukushima.jp/New/gyousei/kyouiku/bunkazai/panf.html) Digitized special exhibitions on medieval Ishikawa Town, centered on the Ishikawa clan.**

shigezane:natunojin.title: Summer Campaign of Osaka
shigezane:natunojin.summary: In Genna 1 (1615), Shigezane took part in the Summer Campaign of the Siege of Osaka. The struggle of the Date forces in this battle is recounted in the memoirs of Kagetsuna Katakura—the so-called "Battle of Domyoji."
shigezane:natunojin.markdown:
In the first year of Genna (1615), Shigezane took part in the Summer Campaign of the Siege of Osaka. The fierce fighting of the Date forces in this battle is recounted in the so-called "Battle of Domyoji," as documented in the memoirs of Kagetsuna Katakura. The accounts in the Date family records are believed to rely almost entirely on these memoirs of Kagetsuna and the head registers passed down within each family.

I will leave the detailed course of the battle to other sites for now and instead introduce some anecdotes about Shigezane passed down during the Summer Campaign. (These are "anecdotes" and not necessarily historical facts—or rather, some might say, "Isn't that a bit fishy?")

## Competing for the vanguard with Munesada Shiroishi (Hakutatsu-ki)

Before the Battle of Domyoji during the Siege of Osaka, a banner-bearer for Munemi Shiroishi overtook one for Shigezane. Shigezane: "Your Kuyo crest is too far forward. Step back." Munemi: "Is this the time to be playing the cool guy on the battlefield?" Shigezane: "I am the vanguard today. If you will not listen, I have no choice but to report this to my lord." Munemi: "As you know, the banners of my Shiroishi house have never trailed behind those of others since the time of Munemi." Then, just as both soldiers had their hands on their swords and a clash seemed imminent, a senior retainer of Munemi's persuaded both sides, saying, "Is this really the time to be bickering?"

## Encouraging Matsumoto Wakasa (Records of the Teizan-ko Family)

There was a retainer of Masamune's named Matsumoto Wakasa. While the Date forces rushed forward, each striving for glory, Wakasa remained motionless. Shigezane Date then urged him, "Hurry up and join the fight and earn some merit!" When Wakasa hesitantly replied, "No, I have not received orders from you, my lord," Shigezane pushed him further, saying, "Geez, just earn some merit and you won't have any complaints. I'll take responsibility, so just go!" Only then did Wakasa finally move. Sure enough, Wakasa earned merit and was praised by Masamune.

(To be expanded upon at a later date. Photo courtesy of Mr./Ms. Nozaki. Description appears on hover.)

Was the fierce general Shigezane actually impaired in his right hand?

Shigezane's father, Sanemoto, whose adoption dispute sparked the Tenbun turmoil across the three provinces of Ou and Echigo. There are mysterious aspects to his origins.

The original page can be found here: [Report on Shigezane Date (Shigezane Zanmai)](http://shigezane.info/majime/nazo/nazo.htm). Links within the text point directly to the pages on the original site as they were during the conversion process. Once corresponding articles are created on Neo Shigezane Zanmai, they will be redirected there accordingly.

shigezane:nenpyou.summary: This is a chronology of Shigezane Date. I have converted the chronology from the original site, "Shigezane Zanmai," into Markdown. From 1539 to 1646, it lists Shigezane's life and the events of the era, along with their sources.

shigezane:nenpyou.markdown:
[View the "Shigezane Date Timeline" by scrolling horizontally here](https://oosawak.github.io/neo-shigezane-zanmai/nenpyou-timeline.html)

## 1539 (Tenbun 8)

- Autumn: Locusts plagued various provinces, crops failed. Sendai: Poor harvest. Great famine. ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 11/18 Major Earthquake ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1540 (Tenbun 9)

- 8/11 Strong winds ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- Autumn: Locusts plagued various provinces, crops failed. Sendai: Poor harvest. Great famine. ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1541 (Tenbun 10)

- 8/11 Strong winds ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1557 (Koji 3)

- August 14: Severe wind and rain at night ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 8/24 Flood ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- Severe crop failure and great famine ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1558 (Eiroku 1)

- Famine ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1561 (Eiroku 4)

- Epidemic. August, Eiroku 3 – May, Eiroku 4. ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1564 (Eiroku 7)

- Crop failure ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1565 (Eiroku 8)

- This year, Terumune succeeded as head of the clan (Family Records)
- That year, famine ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 6/19 Tanemune died at age 78

## 1566 (Eiroku 9)

- 1/10 Pledge received from Ashina Moriuji (Jike Records)

## 1567 (Eiroku 10)

- 2/11 Death of Ashina, principal wife of Tanemune (Jike Records)
- 3/7 Head of the Rusu Family, Masakage (Family Records)
- 8/3 Birth of Masamune (Jike Records)

## 1568 (Eiroku 11)

- This year: Shigezane born (Seshin Kafu), at Omori Castle (Tokiwa Sadaken Documents)

## 1570 (Genki 1)

- 4/4 Rebellion of Munetoki Nakano, Hisanaka Makino, and Yoshinao Nitta (Jike Kiroku)
- Early September: Nakano and Makino petitioned for reinstatement through Harumune and Sanemoto, but were denied (Jike Records)

## 1571 (Genki 2)

- That year, in recognition of his achievements in the battle against Soma, Motomune Watari was granted the Takesuzume crest (Jike Kiroku).

## 1572 (Genki 3)

- 7/7 Toraya enters Shifuku-ji (Jike Records)

## 1573 (Tensho 1)

- Fall of the Ashikaga Shogunate
- 12/28 Oda Nobunaga sends a letter to Terumune. The first documentary record of the establishment of ties with the Oda clan (Dai Nihon Komonjo, Date Family Documents 291).
- In this year, Gensho-in was born (Wakuya Date Documents 11)

## 1574 (Tensho 2)

- 2/21 Nobunaga's letter from late last year arrives (Seizan Koji Family Records)
- 4/3 Sanemoto captures Hachome Castle (Seizan-ko Jike Kiroku)

## 1575 (Tensho 3)

- Intercalary January 24, Great Earthquake ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- Autumn: Terumune Date sends horses and hawks to Nobunaga

## 1577 (Tensho 5)

- 11/15 Masamune's coming-of-age ceremony (Jike Records). Shigezane served as the sword-bearer. (Date Hikan)

## 1579 (Tensho 7)

- Poor harvest that year ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 6/17-6/26 Heavy rain. Numerous people and horse messengers were dispatched due to flooding in Tome, Sanuma, Masubuchi, Momo, and Wakuya (History of Watari Town) ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- That year, Shigezane underwent his coming-of-age ceremony at Omori Castle. His eboshi-oya was Terumune (Tokiwa Sadaken Documents).

## 1582 (Tensho 10)

- June 2: The Honno-ji Incident

## 1584 (Tensho 12)

- 10/6 Ashina Moritaka killed by a favorite retainer at Kurokawa Castle
- October: Masamune assumes headship of the clan (Shigezane-ki)
- October: Shigezane receives a license in Tenryu (Masamune Date Transmission Documents B-16, B-26)
- That year, Shigezane succeeded as head of the family. Sanemoto retired to Hachichome Castle.
- Ouchi Sadatsuna submitted. Spent the New Year in Yonezawa. (Shigezane-ki)

## 1585 (Tensho 13)

- January: Ouchi Sadatsuna returns to Obama. (Shigezane-ki)
- 5/2 Harada Samanosuke, via Sarukura-goe, headed for Shibano Danjo's residence. (Shigezane-ki)
- 5/3 Masamune marches out to Hibara. (Shigezane-ki)
- 5/8 Masamune attacks Oshio Castle. Shigezane departs Omori. (Shigezane-ki)
- 5/9 Shigezane took up positions at Hibara. He sent a letter of intrigue to Inawashiro and returned to Omori that same day. Did he stay overnight in Tsunaki? (Jike Records)
- 5/12 Harada Samanosuke, via Sarukura-goe, to Shibano Danjo's residence. (Aizu Shika Goko)
- 5/13 Masamune marches out from Hibara. (Aizu Four Houses Combined Study)
- 5/13 Reply from Inawashiro arrived at Masamune's camp. Masamune dispatched Mine Shikibu and Nanamiya Hoki to Shigezane in Omori. Both envoys stayed in Omori (Jike Records).
- Following this, Shigezane dispatched Sanzoken to Inawashiro via Tsuchiyu (Jike Records).
- May 14: Tsunami struck Tokura Village, Motoyoshi District. ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 6/8 Shigezane [responds](#/post/shigezane/t13-6-8) to Morikuni Inawashiro (Sendai Bukan).
- 6/11 [Reply](#/post/shigezane/t13-6-11) from Inawashiro (Sendai Bukan).
- Following this, Masamune accepted only the terms of Inawashiro and dispatched the two envoys to Shigezane. The two envoys then returned to Hibara (Jike Records).
- 6/28 Withdrawal from Hibara. Nobuyasu Goto stationed at Hibara (Jike Records)
- July: Hideyoshi appointed Kanpaku
- 7/上 Shigezane advises Masamune to subdue the Ouchi. Begins machinations against Aoki Shuri (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 7/2 Hideyoshi issues a document to Motonobu Endo (Saito Hoonkai Documents)
- 8/5 Aoki Shuri invited the son of the Ouchi family elder to Karimatsu. (Shigezane-ki)
- 8/6 Aoki Shuri, son of the Ouchi chief retainer, goes hunting. At midnight, Shuri captures the son of the Ouchi chief retainer (Shigezane-ki).
- Intercalary August 7: Shigezane reported to Masamune that Aoki Shuri had severed ties with the Ouchi. Masamune stationed Koyanagawa Morimune, Shiroishi Munemi, Harada Munetoki, and Hamada Kagetaka near Karimatsu, and had Shigezane encamp at Tatsukoyama (Jike Records).
- Intercalary August 12: Masamune departed for Yonezawa and took up positions at Sugime. Shigezane dispatched messengers Aoki Shuri and another to Sugime (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki).
- Intercalary August 17: Masamune moved to Kawamata. Met with Tamura Kiyoaki at Warabidaira (Jike Records).
- Intercalary August 23: Siege of Kotemori suspended due to heavy rain (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- Intercalary August 24: Battle of Kotemori Castle begins. (Jike Records) (Shigezane-ki)
- Intercalary August 25: Attack on Kotemori Castle (Shigezane-ki)
- Intercalary August 26: Shigezane advocated for a relocation of the camp during deliberations. (Jike Records) (Shigezane-ki)
- Morning of intercalary August 27: Shigezane moved his camp without Masamune's permission. Kotemori Castle fell. (Jike Records)
- In the early hours of the intercalary 8th, 29th, Masamune departed for Shozan. Shigezane dispatched retainers ahead to establish a camp. Reports arrived that the fortification had fallen. Shigezane entered the fortification and reported this to Masamune. Masamune rested at the fortification (Jike Kiroku).
- 9/22 Masamune departed for Tsukidate and headed for Kurokago. Shigezane, Munemi, Kojuro, and Sakurada Motochika remained behind (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 9/23 Masamune rests at Kurokago (Shigezane-ki)
- 9/24 Masamune attacked "Kara-no-uchi" from Kurokago ([Shigezane-ki](#/post/shigezane/shigezaneki-9)). Together with Nara and others, he advanced from Tsukidate toward the Kose River. (Katakura Daidai-ki, Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 9/25 Masamune attacked Iwakado and returned to Kurokago (Shigezane-ki). At night, he withdrew from Obama. (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/6 Hatakeyama Yoshitsugu begged for surrender at Terumune's camp in Miyanomori. Terumune went to Masamune's camp in Kohama that night. Shigezane joined the negotiations and conveyed Yoshitsugu's intentions. (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/7 Yoshitsugu requests an audience with Terumune through Shigezane. Terumune meets with Yoshitsugu at Shigezane's camp (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/8 Shigezane mediated a request for gratitude from Yoshitsugu to Terumune at Miyamori and attended the audience. Yoshitsugu seized Terumune and killed him at Takadahara. (Jiike Records) At night, Masamune marched toward Takada. Honmiya, Tamanoi, and Shibukawa surrendered of their own accord (Shigezane-ki).
- Early morning on 10/9, Masamune returns to Obama. At night, the remains of Terumune enter Obama (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki).
- 10/15 Masamune attacked Nihonmatsu. Shigezane took up a position at Ihoda and fought the castle garrison (Jike Kiroku). A strong wind blew from midnight (Shigezane-ki).
- 10/16 Snow all day (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/17 Snow all day (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/18 Snow all day (Shigezane-ki)
- 10/21 Attack on Nihonmatsu aborted due to heavy snow. Troops withdrawn (Jike Records)
- Around 11/10: Various generals of the Sendo marched on Sukagawa (Shigezane-ki)
- 11/10– Shigezane, from Shibukawa to Iwakado. After participating in discussions, moved to Nukazawa at night. (Jike Records)
- 11/16 The generals of Sendo established a field camp at Maeda Sawanami (Shigezane-ki)
- 11/17 Battle of Hitotoribashi. Masamune returns to Iwakado. Shigezane receives a [letter of commendation](#/post/shigezane/29) from Masamune (Jike Kiroku). ([Shigezane-ki](#/post/shigezane/shigezaneki-15)) (Masamune-ki)
- 11/18 Shigezane moved to Motomiya before dawn. After confirming the enemy's retreat, he reported to Masamune at Iwakado. (Shigezane-ki) Masamune marched to Motomiya and granted rewards for merit. (Jike Kiroku)
- 11/19 Masamune encamped at Iwakado (Shigezane-ki)
- 11/20 Masamune encamped at Iwakado (Shigezane-ki)
- 11/21 Masamune returned to Obama and spent the New Year. (Shigezane-ki)
- 12/11 [Hour of the Dog, fire at Shibukawa Castle. Shigezane burned his right hand](#/post/shigezane/masamuneki3-11) (Masamune Chronicles)
- That year, a great famine (History of Watari Town) ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))

## 1586 (Tensho 14)

- 1/1 [Battle of Shibukawa](#/post/shigezane/sibukawa) (Family Records) ([Shigezane-ki](#/post/shigezane/shigezaneki-17)) ([Masamune-ki](#/post/shigezane/masamuneki3-1))
- 1/2 Shigezane sends his head to Masamune. (Masamune-ki & [Masamune Documents Supplement 135?](#/post/shigezane/h135))
- 1/4 Masamune to Shigezane [letter?](#/post/shigezane/h135). Presents a sword and a kosode. Southern loyalty. (Supplement to the Masamune Documents)
- February: Minowa Genban conspired with Masamune, but was suppressed by the castle forces. (Shigezane-ki)
- During this period, Masamune was in poor health (Shigezane-ki)
- April: Masamune attacked Nihonmatsu Castle. (Shigezane-ki)
- 4/19 Hideyoshi issued a document to Satake Yoshishige instructing him to ensure the safety of Ashina and Date (Uesugi Family Documents 835)
- 7/5 A peace agreement in Nihonmatsu was reached through the mediation of Soma. Sanemoto, Motomune Watari, and Munemi Shiroishi also served as intermediaries (Jike Kiroku).
- 7/16 Nihonmatsu surrendered. Shigezane took possession of the castle, built a temporary residence in the honmaru, and served as castle warden. (Katakura Daidai-ki) (Jike Kiroku) (Shigezane-ki)
- 7/Part 2: Yamagami Dogyu conveys Hideyoshi's intention for "peace" to Oshu (Ou Shioki in the Toyotomi Regime, p. 42)
- 8/12 Kagetsuna Katakura was granted Nihonmatsu. (Jike Records)
- 9/13 Shigezane transferred to Nihonmatsu. Kagetsuna Katakura to Omori. (Family Records)
- 10/27 Tokugawa Ieyasu met with Hideyoshi at Osaka Castle and declared his submission.
- November: Kamewakamaru Ashina died.
- 12/15 Masamune to Shigezane [Letter](#/post/shigezane/88). Regarding Sowa and Tamura, and Shigezane's marriage. (Masamune Documents)
- December? Shigezane married the daughter of Shigemune Watari. (Jike Records)

## 1587 (Tensho 15)

- 1/4 Masamune to Shigezane [letter?](#/post/shigezane/h135). Presents a sword and a kosode. Southern loyalty. (Supplement to the Masamune Documents)
- March: Yoshihiro Shirakawa, second son of Yoshishige Satake, succeeded the Ashina clan.
- 4/7 Masamune visits the bedridden Sanemoto. (Jike Records)
- 4/16 Shigemoto died. (Jike Records)
- 5/1 Koyanagawa Muneshige, as an envoy for Shigezane, to Masamune (Jike Kiroku)
- 5/9 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/108). Regarding the regulations for the Nihonmatsu border. (Masamune Documents)
- May 10: Major Earthquake in Sendai (History of Watari Town) ([Miyagi Prefecture Disaster Chronology](http://www.pref.miyagi.jp/kikitaisaku/6-1-1(1).pdf))
- 7/11 Shigezane's territory, Naeshiroda, attacked. Shigezane sends a letter to Masamune regarding his response (Jike Kiroku).
- 7/13 Masamune's [reply](#/post/shigezane/122) to Shigezane regarding the Naeshiroda matter (Jike Records)
- 9/10 Around this time, news arrived of Hideyoshi's successful conquest of Kyushu. Hakuzoken and Dokaisai departed Yonezawa as mourners for Hideyoshi (Tensho Nikki).
- 9/24 Masamune to Shigezane [Reply](#/post/shigezane/130). Matters concerning Naeshiroda, the Motomiya construction, and the Tamura matter (Jike Records)
- 9/29 Masamune to Shigezane: [Reply](#/post/shigezane/135). Matters concerning Ouchi and Tamura. (Masamune Documents)
- 10/14 Masamune [reported](#/post/shigezane/143) to Shigezane that Ayugai had fallen. (Masamune Documents)
- October: Yoshimitsu Mogami conquers Shonai.
- 11/19 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/152). Regarding the matter of Kokubun, and the matter of Sugime. (Masamune Documents)
- 12/3 Hideyoshi issues a direct decree of "Somuji" (Date Family Documents 986)
- 12/10 Masamune to Shigezane [Reply](#/post/shigezane/162). The matter of Yasukogashima (Jike Records)
- 12/Mid: Shigezane dispatches Endo Suruga to Masamune. Masamune gives instructions to Endo Suruga regarding the Tamura matter (Jike Kiroku).
- That year, Ouchi Sadatsuna expressed his intention to surrender through Shigezane and Kagetsuna. (Jike Records)

## 1588 (Tensho 16)

- 1/7 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/167). Regarding the matter of the southern route. Have Endo and Haneda come. (Masamune Documents)
- 1/15 Haneda Umanosuke attended Masamune's tea ceremony. (Date Tensho Nikki) (Jike Kiroku)
- 1/17 The Shigezane family received sake from Masamune at Takaya. Five of them were also granted clothing. (Date Tensho Nikki) (Jike Kiroku)
- 2/12, Hour of the Ox: Ouchi Sadatsuna attacked Naeshiroda and slew Honnai Shusui (Jike Kiroku, Masamune-ki, Shigezane-ki)
- During this period, Shigezane appealed to Shigezane, citing petitions from Katahira Chikatsuna—who had entered service—as well as the Honnai Shusui clan and others. Shigezane agreed. Shigezane, Kojuro, and Takano Iki held private discussions and reported the matter to Masamune. Masamune also agreed. A letter arrived from Ouchi requesting fiefs on behalf of Shigezane (Jike Kiroku).
- 2/27 Masamune grants land holdings to Ouchi on the condition that Katahira enters their service (Jike Kiroku)
- 3/1 Hakuzoken and Dokaisai returned.
- 3/8 Hour of the Boar: Masamune sends a [letter](#/post/shigezane/216) to Shigezane. Reports on the Osaki area and the matter of Naeshiroda. (Jike Records)
- Prior to this, Shigezane, Takakura Omi, and Ishikawa Danjo reported to Masamune of their rebellious intentions.
- 3/12 Masamune issued instructions to Kojuro via letter. Regarding Ishikawa Danjo: to consult with Shigezane and investigate. (Jike Records)
- 3/12-13– Enemy scouting activity at Tamai in Shigezane's territory (Jike Kiroku) (Masamune-ki)
- 3/21 Masamune dispatches Iki Takano to Shigezane (Jike Records)
- Evening of March 22: Intelligence reached Shigezane that a courtesy visit to Tamai was scheduled for tonight. Shigezane set out (Jike Records).
- 3/23 Early morning arrived, but no sign of the enemy. Shigezane withdrew. Around noon, the enemy attacked. Tamai conducted reconnaissance.
- Prior to this, Shigezane and Kojuro coordinated the positions of Ouchi and Katahira (Jike Kiroku)
- 4/1 Masamune, upon the assurance of Shigezane and Kagetsuna, granted a fief of 60 kanmon to Ouchi Sadatsuna. (Jike Records)
- 4/3 Kagetsuna to Nihonmatsu. Waits alongside Shigezane for the appearance of Ouchi Ujitsuna.
- On the night of 4/5, Bizen nephew Kajinai Danjo sent a messenger to Kagetsuna's lodgings. Shigezane and Kagetsuna proceeded to Motomiya to welcome Ouchi Ujitsuna. (Masamune-ki)
- 4/6 Shigezane and Kagetsuna met with the Ouchi. As the attempt to sever ties with Katahira Chikatsuna had failed, Shigezane, Kagetsuna, and Munemi attacked Yasukogashima. The enemy did not respond. (Katakura Daidai-ki) (Jike Kiroku)
- 4/7 Shigezane, Kagetsuna, and Munemi Shiroishi attacked Yasukogashima. The enemy did not respond. At Shiomatsu, Ishikawa Danjo rebelled. Munemi returned to Shiomatsu (Masamune-ki).
- Shigezane presented a bay horse to Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- During this time, Ouchi Sadatsuna requested an audience with Masamune through Shigezane. Shigezane had Endo Suruga accompany Ouchi. (Jike Records)
- 4/8 Kagetsuna, along with Iki Takano, was presented to Ouchi. (Jike Records)
- 4/9 Kagetsuna returns to Omori from Yasukogashima (Masamune-ki)
- 4/12 Ishikawa Danjo conducted reconnaissance westward in the territory of Munemi Shiroishi. Shigezane, hearing the sound of muskets, set out. He did not arrive in time for the battle. Munemi hosted Shigezane at Miyamori. (Masamune-ki).
- 4/15 Ishikawa Danjo conducted reconnaissance in the territory of Munemi Shiroishi. Shigezane, hearing the sound of muskets, marched out. He did not arrive in time for the battle. Munemi hosted Shigezane at Miyamori. (Jike Records)
- 4/18 Battle of Asaka. (Jike Records)
- 5/1 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/252). Regarding Ishikawa Danjo. (Masamune Documents)
- 5/2 Ishikawa Subjugation Proclamation (Jike Records)
- 5/6 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/257). Regarding Ishikawa Danjo. (Masamune Documents)
- 5/14 Masamune departed Yonezawa to subjugate Ishikawa Danjo.
- 5/15 Masamune went to Sugime to meet Princess Kubo. Shigezane also went to Sugime. They returned together. Shigezane was granted a white twill kimono by Masamune (Date Tensho Nikki).
- 5/16 Noon: Masamune went to Sugime to meet Princess Kubo. Shigezane also went to Sugime. They returned together. Shigezane was granted a white twill kimono by Masamune (Jike Records).
- May 16, midnight: Masamune served a meal to Shigezane. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 5/17 Shigezane participated in a discussion with Masamune. Masamune showed Shigezane and Munemi Shiroishi his prized horses. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 5/17 Shigezane and Munemi visit Masamune. Midnight: Shigezane receives a meal from Masamune (Jike Records).
- 5/18 Shigezane participates in the council (Jike Records)
- 5/20 Masamune to Tsukidate. In the evening, the attending retainers took up positions in the field. (Jike Records)
- 5/22 Masamune attacked Kotemori Castle. At night, Shigezane returned to Nihonmatsu as a precaution (Jike Kiroku).
- 5/23 Shigezane, from Nihonmatsu to Kotemori. Returned to Nihonmatsu as the attack was suspended due to rain (Jiike Records).
- 5/23 Enemy scouts sent to Tamai. Shigezane slew three and proceeded to Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 5/24 Shigezane, from Nihonmatsu to Kotemori. Reported that he cut down grass at Tamai (Jike Records).
- 5/26 Due to poor weather, the attack on Kotemori Castle was aborted. Masamune proceeded to Omori. (Jike Records)
- 5/28 Shigezane met with Masamune in Omori. They shared dinner. Haneda Umanosuke accompanied them. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 5/29 Shigezane visited Masamune. In the evening, Masamune entertained Shigezane. Haneda also joined them (Jike Records).
- On the night of May 30, Shigezane went to Masamune at Omori. Reported on Tamura. (Katakura Daidai-ki) Shigezane and Munemi went to Masamune. Discussed the matter of Tamura. (Jike Kiroku)
- Intercalary May 1: Report from Munemi of Miyamori (Jike Records)
- Intercalary May 2: Shigezane reports the safety of Miyamori (Jike Records). Shigezane sends a messenger to Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- Intercalary May 5: Shigezane dispatched a messenger to Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki) (Jike Kiroku)
- Intercalary May 11: Soma Yoshitane sent word to Tamura of his intention to enter Miharu Castle from Tsukiyama. (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 12: Tamura refused Soma Yoshitane's entry into the castle. Reported the matter to Obama. At the hour of the Boar, Shiroishi Wakasa reported the matter to Masamune in Omori. Masamune immediately set out. (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 13: Masamune arrived at Miyamori. Attacked Tsukiyama. Sent Shigezane to Shiraiwa in Tamura. (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 14: Masamune attacks Tsukiyama. (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 16: Masamune attacked Kotemori. Shigezane also joined the battle, tasked with holding the Tsukiyama area. The castle fell. (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 17: Masamune attacked Tamura Hikoshichiro at Okura Castle; Tamura initiated negotiations with Urayuki. Masamune returned to Miyamori. The remaining forces set up camp in a place called "Nishi." (Masamune-ki)
- Intercalary May 18: While Masamune was marching his troops to Ishizawa in Tamura, Tamura Hikoshichiro surrendered. Although he requested lodging in the "west," as there were no houses, he set up camp in the mountains to the east. At night, there was thunder. Tsukiyama, Ishizawa, and Hyakumeki fell of their own accord.
- Intercalary May 25: Shigezane goes to Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- Intercalary May: Kanayama Sosen, envoy delivering the Edict of General Peace, visits Mogami Yoshimitsu.

- 7/7 Kubota Fort duty: Shigezane, Munemi Shiroishi.

- 8/3 Shigezane visits Masamune. Is served a meal. (Date Tensho Nikki)

- 8/18 Shigezane joined Masamune for breakfast. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 8/26 Shigezane visits Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- August: Yoshioki Muto and Shigenaga Honjo recapture Shonai from Yoshimitsu Mogami
- 9/13 Shigezane visits Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)

## 1589 (Tensho 17)

- Late February: Shigezane informed Kagetsuna of the above. Kagetsuna confirmed Masamune's intentions, and Shigezane met with Katahira in Horiuchi, Asaka District, to discuss severing ties. (Katakura Daidai-ki)
- 3/19 Masamune to Shigezane: [Letter](#/post/shigezane/393). Regarding the Katahira matter. (Masamune Documents)

- 4/27 Shigezane, along with Chikatsuna Katahira, went to see Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 4/28 Shigezane returns. (Date Tensho Nikki)

- 5/29 Shigezane participated in a consultation with Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 6/1 Returned to Sanzoken Omori. Masamune ordered Kagetsuna and Shigezane to proceed to Inawashiro. Shigezane departed Nihonmatsu and stayed overnight at Arai. (Katakura Daidai-ki)

- 6/15 Shigezane to Masamune (Date Tensho Nikki)
- 6/16 Shigezane visits Masamune. (Date Tensho Nikki)

## 1590 (Tensho 18)

- 11/24 Rescued Kimura Yoshikiyo and his son from Sanuma-ochi.

## 1591 (Tensho 19)

- 1/1 Shigezane, as a hostage, went to Nasho Castle, where Ujisato Gamo was stationed. Accompanied Ujisato on his return to Kurokawa.

## 1595 (Bunroku 4)

- Around May–June, Masamune departed from the Jurakuya residence and headed for Iwadeyama. (Katakura Daidai-ki)

## 1596 (Bunroku 5/Keicho 1)

## 1598 (Keicho 2)

- 8/18 Hideyoshi died.
- This year? Shigezane fled (Jike Records) (Tohan Yajo).
- October? Akimitsu Ishikawa transferred to Kakuda.

## Nihonmatsu Castle

Located within the walls of [Nihonmatsu City](http://www.city.nihonmatsu.fukushima.jp/index-1.html), Fukushima Prefecture. A mountain castle situated on Shirahata-ge Mine. It was built during the Oei era by the Hatakeyama clan, who served as the Oshu Tandai. From September of Tensho 14 to Tensho 19, Shigezane resided there. That said, as it was a period when there was little time to rest amidst the fighting, it is believed that the castle was largely left to the castle warden. Kagetsuna Katakura subsequently became the castle lord. Incidentally, after the conquest of Nihonmatsu, Kagetsuna Katakura also served as the castle keeper until the rewards for meritorious service were granted. It appears that the honmaru of Nihonmatsu Castle was used solely for military purposes until this period. The main gate (ote) was located between the Minowa-kan and Shinjo-kan, and its orientation differed from that of the present day. Under Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Ou Shioki, the Toyotomi army stayed there, and structures believed to be temporary dwellings from that time have been unearthed. During the Edo period, the castle was developed as an early modern fortification by the Kato and Niwa clans. [Please also refer to this site](http://arch.ce.nihon-u.ac.jp/~kano/kano/eco-01/history0.html#top)

At that time, Shigezane's territory included Hachichome, Naeshiroda, Tamai, and Motomiya. (Masamune-ki)

## Aizu Kurokawa Castle

Remained in the castle as the castle warden during Masamune's campaign at Odawara.
